If sauce is too thin, simmer on stovetop to reduce slightly.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve lamb shanks with the rich sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, braise the lamb shanks a day in advance and reheat gently. The flavors will deepen.

recipes.recipe_name: Ethiopian Spiced Milk Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: Four individual Ethiopian Spiced Milk Tartlets are casually arranged on a well-used wooden dining table. Each tartlet, approximately 10-12 cm in diameter, sits on a simple, earthy-toned ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The shortcrust pastry shells are golden-brown, showcasing a rustic, slightly uneven edge, indicating homemade preparation. Inside, the custard filling is a pale, creamy yellow, smooth and set, with a gentle sheen. A generous, uneven dusting of white icing sugar covers the surface of each custard, creating a soft, inviting appearance. The tartlets are presented as whole, modest portions, inviting a comfortable, shared experience. Beside one tartlet, a traditional Ethiopian coffee cup (finjal) with its distinct shape and pattern, filled with dark coffee, is visible. A woven mesob (traditional Ethiopian basket table) or a simple, textured fabric runner in warm tones subtly grounds the scene. The lighting is warm and cozy, suggesting a family kitchen or a relaxed dining area, with natural light filtering in. The overall presentation is homely and unpretentious, emphasizing comfort and the inviting warmth of the spiced dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly brewed Ethiopian coffee (buna), traditionally served in small cups (finjal) after a coffee ceremony.
Offer alongside a glass of Ethiopian spiced tea (shai) for a comforting beverage pairing.
Present on a traditional mesob (woven basket table) for a communal, authentic feel.
instructions: Combine flour, icing sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Add diced cold butter. Rub butter into flour mixture with fingertips until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add ice water, mixing until dough just comes together. Do not overmix.
Form dough into a flat disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Roll out chilled dough on a lightly floured surface to 3mm thickness.
Cut out four circles using a round cutter larger than your tartlet molds.
Gently press dough circles into four individual tartlet molds (approx. 10-12 cm diameter). Trim excess dough.
Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper. Fill with baking beans or rice.
Bake for 15 minutes. Remove baking beans and parchment. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until lightly golden.
Remove from oven. Let cool completely in molds.
In a saucepan, combine milk, corn syrup, butter, icing sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves.
Heat over medium heat, stirring until butter is melted and sugar is dissolved. Bring to a gentle simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk egg yolks and cornstarch until smooth.
Slowly temper egg yolk mixture by whisking in about 100ml of the hot milk mixture.
Pour tempered egg yolk mixture back into the saucepan with remaining milk.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a whisk, until custard thickens to a pudding-like consistency. Do not boil vigorously.
Remove from heat. Strain custard through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl to remove any lumps or spice solids.
Cover surface of custard directly with cling film to prevent a skin from forming. Let cool slightly.
Pour warm custard evenly into the cooled tartlet shells.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until custard is firm and set.
Carefully remove tartlets from molds.
Dust generously with icing sugar before serving.
notes: For an extra layer of flavor, you can toast the whole spices (cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves) lightly before grinding them or infusing them in the milk.
Ensure the custard is thoroughly chilled for the best texture and to prevent it from being too runny when served.

recipes.recipe_name: Enguday Fasoli Wot (Mushroom and Kidney Bean Stew)
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Enguday Fasoli Wot is presented in a traditional, rustic Ethiopian clay bowl. The stew is a deep, rich reddish-brown, glistening with Niter Kibbeh. Visible pieces of tender, sliced mushrooms and whole kidney beans are suspended in the thick, savory sauce. A few thin slices of fresh green chili are scattered on top for a vibrant color contrast. A large, circular piece of spongy, bubbly injera is placed next to the bowl, slightly overlapping, ready for tearing. The setting is a warm-toned, well-used wooden dining table. The lighting is soft and inviting, mimicking natural kitchen light. A simple, dark-colored cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, maintaining focus on the comforting, homely dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with injera, used to scoop up the stew.
Traditionally eaten communally from a large platter, but here presented as an individual portion.
Often accompanied by other wots or salads for a varied meal.

ingredients.name: Niter Kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) or vegetable oil

instructions: Heat Niter Kibbeh or oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onions. Cook for 10-15 minutes until very soft and translucent, stirring frequently.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in berbere spice mix and tomato paste. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing spices to bloom.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and soften.
Stir in drained kidney beans and hot water or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 20-25 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot.
notes: For a vegan version, use vegetable oil instead of Niter Kibbeh.
Adjust berbere quantity to control spice level.
This wot thickens as it cools; add a splash of water or broth if reheating.
traditional_techniques: Beshela (slow cooking onions until very soft)

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Tomato and Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of golden-brown, bone-in chicken thigh is centered on a deep, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken is generously coated and surrounded by a rich, reddish-brown sauce, thick with tender, caramelized onion slices. The sauce has a rustic, unctuous texture. Freshly chopped parsley, bright green, is scattered over the chicken and sauce, providing a vibrant contrast. The dish is presented on a worn, dark wooden dining table. A simple fork and knife are placed to the right, with a loosely folded, light-colored linen napkin nearby. A small bowl of mashed potatoes sits to the side. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a cozy, lived-in kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes or crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot. Cook on low heat on the stovetop or in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Choose a beer that is not too bitter or hoppy. Amber ales or lagers work well.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Parsley Salata with Berbere Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Ethiopian Tomato and Parsley Salata is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl, its colors popping against the earthy tones of a well-used wooden dining table. Diced red tomatoes and finely chopped fresh green parsley are generously mixed with delicate slivers of red onion and a hint of dried chili flakes. The vegetables are coated in a light, reddish-orange berbere dressing, which glistens subtly. The salad fills the bowl naturally, with some components slightly overlapping, creating an inviting, unpretentious mound. Beside the bowl, a few pieces of spongy, grey-brown injera bread are casually arranged, ready for scooping. A simple, off-white cloth napkin lies nearby. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural freshness and inviting texture of the dish. The overall presentation is homely and authentic, reflecting a traditional Ethiopian family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing side dish with various Ethiopian wots (stews) or tibs (sautéed meats).
Traditionally eaten with injera, using pieces of the flatbread to scoop up the salad.
Often part of a larger communal meal served on a mesob (basket table).
instructions: In a large bowl, combine diced tomatoes, finely chopped red onion, finely chopped parsley, and dried chili flakes.
For the dressing, in a small bowl, whisk together minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, olive oil, berbere spice blend, and salt.
Pour the dressing over the chopped vegetables. Toss gently to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve immediately, or chill briefly for flavors to meld.
traditional_techniques: Mise en place (preparing all ingredients before cooking/assembly)
Using traditional spice blends like Berbere

recipes.recipe_name: Revani me Kakao kai Fermentomeno Sirópi Lemoniou (Revani with Cocoa and Fermented Lemon Syrup)
recipes.visual_description: A single square slice of 'Revani me Kakao kai Fermentomeno Sirópi Lemoniou' is precisely centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The cake displays a moist, golden-yellow semolina crumb, subtly marbled with rich cocoa and cinnamon swirls. The top surface glistens from the absorbed fermented lemon syrup. A single, thin, dehydrated lemon wheel, made from a zero-waste approach, rests delicately on one corner of the cake. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of a green plant visible, emphasizing the dish's natural beauty and sustainable ethos. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the cake slice, creating an unforced, elegant composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature as a dessert or with coffee.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Lemon Syrup (3-5 days prior): Combine 200 ml water, 200 g sugar, and lemon juice in a clean glass jar. Add finely chopped lemon peels. Stir well. Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Let sit at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Stir daily. Taste for a slight tang and reduced sweetness. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Make Brown Butter: Melt 150 g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring often, until butter solids turn golden brown and smell nutty. Immediately pour into a heatproof bowl to stop cooking. Let cool slightly.
Preheat Oven & Prepare Pan: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20x20 cm square baking pan.
Combine Wet Ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk 150 g sugar, 3 eggs, 150 g Greek yogurt, brown butter, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Combine Dry Ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk 200 g semolina and 10 g baking powder.
Form Batter: Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Create Swirl: Scoop one-third of the batter into a small bowl. Stir in 15 g cocoa powder and 5 g ground cinnamon until uniform.
Layer Batter: Pour the plain semolina batter into the prepared pan. Spoon the cocoa-cinnamon batter over the plain batter. Gently swirl with a knife or skewer for a marbled effect.
Bake Cake: Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Soak Cake: Remove cake from oven. Immediately pour the cooled fermented lemon syrup evenly over the warm cake.
Cool & Serve: Let cake cool completely in the pan on a wire rack. Cut into 4 square portions.
notes: The fermented lemon syrup adds a unique tang and complexity, enhancing the cake's flavor profile.
Ensure lemon peels for fermentation are from organic, unwaxed lemons.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom, Caramelized Onion, and Roasted Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table under warm kitchen light. A bed of vibrant mixed salad greens forms the base. Arranged on top are tender, browned slices of sautéed cremini mushrooms, deeply golden caramelized red onion strands, and burst, slightly shriveled roasted cherry tomato halves. Each vegetable retains its distinct shape and natural color. A light, glistening balsamic vinaigrette coats the ingredients. Fresh green parsley is scattered on top for color and freshness. The presentation is unpretentious and hearty, reflecting a comforting home-cooked meal. A simple, sturdy fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed linen napkin. The bowl is adequately filled, allowing all components to be clearly visible without overcrowding.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200 0C.
On a baking sheet, toss halved cherry tomatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15 minutes, or until slightly softened.
In a large pan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced red onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Remove from pan.
In the same pan, add another 15ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 15ml olive oil, balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper for the dressing.
In a large serving bowl, combine roasted tomatoes, caramelized onions, and sautéed mushrooms.
Add mixed salad greens and chopped parsley to the bowl. Pour dressing over the salad.
Gently toss to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Mushroom Savory Patties
recipes.visual_description: The image displays several golden-brown Homestyle Chicken and Mushroom Savory Patties, casually arranged on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The patties are roughly circular, 2-3 cm thick, and have a visibly crispy, textured crust from pan-frying. Flecks of finely diced mushrooms and parsley are visible within the patty mixture. A few fresh parsley leaves are scattered loosely on and around the patties as a functional garnish, adding a touch of green. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. Soft, warm overhead lighting illuminates the food, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the comforting, homemade appeal. A casually folded, plain linen napkin sits beside the plate. The overall scene is simple, unpretentious, and inviting, like a snack served in a family kitchen.
instructions: Finely mince chicken breast. Finely dice onion, mushrooms, and deseeded tomato. Mince garlic.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and diced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and brown.
Transfer cooked vegetables to a large bowl. Let cool slightly.
Add minced chicken, diced tomato, egg, breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix well until combined.
Form the mixture into 12-16 small, flattened patties, about 2-3 cm thick.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Cook patties in batches for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Provençal Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests on a clean white porcelain plate. Its crisp, herb-dusted skin gleams under natural light. Beside it, a generous portion of vibrant Provençal vegetables is artfully arranged. Diced courgette, aubergine, and bell pepper, along with finely diced red onion and halved cherry tomatoes, display a medley of greens, purples, and reds. These tender-crisp vegetables are gently coated in a light, savory sauce that pools subtly around the base. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley, adding a final touch of green. The overall presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, evoking a modern bistro ambiance with soft, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette
Serve with small roasted potatoes
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt, pepper, and Herbes de Provence.
Heat 15 mL olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 mL olive oil to the pan. Sauté finely diced red onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, diced courgette, diced aubergine, and diced bell pepper. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add halved cherry tomatoes, white wine (if using), and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to reduce slightly.
Season vegetable mixture with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to the pan to warm through, spooning sauce over it.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Heart and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl is filled with a rich, dark brown Hearty Beef Heart and Vegetable Stew. Generous, irregular chunks of tender beef heart are nestled among vibrant orange carrot slices, soft white potato cubes, and softened pieces of onion and celery. The stew's sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to the ingredients, with a slight sheen from reduction. A few fresh, bright green parsley leaves are coarsely chopped and sprinkled over the top as a simple, functional garnish. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. Beside the bowl, a simple, everyday silver spoon rests casually. The setting is illuminated by warm, cozy overhead kitchen lighting, creating a comforting and inviting atmosphere. The background subtly hints at a lived-in kitchen, perhaps with a blurred ceramic mug or a spice jar, maintaining focus on the homely dish. The portion is a single, hearty individual serving, filling the bowl generously but not overflowing.
instructions: Trim beef heart. Remove all fat and connective tissue. Cut into 2.5 cm chunks.
Pat beef heart chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Toss with flour until lightly coated.
Peel and dice onion into 1.5 cm pieces. Peel and slice carrots into 1 cm thick rounds. Dice celery into 1 cm pieces. Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef heart chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef heart and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return seared beef heart to the pot. Pour in beef broth. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Bring the stew to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef heart is very tender.
Stir in diced potatoes. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 20-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the stew has thickened.
Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Rice and Apple Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: The Spiced Rice and Apple Croquettes are presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, arranged in an organic, slightly asymmetrical cluster of five to six pieces. Each croquette is a golden-brown cylinder, approximately 5 cm long, with a visibly crispy, textured breadcrumb coating. The interior, subtly revealed at a broken end, shows a soft, pale mixture flecked with darker spices and tiny white rice grains. Finely diced green apple pieces are visible upon closer inspection. A small, creamy white Mint-Yogurt Dip is placed alongside in a separate, small ceramic bowl. A light scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped coriander leaves garnishes the croquettes. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface with a subtly textured cotton napkin folded beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the golden crispness and fresh garnishes. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing the snack in an approachable, professional manner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a cooling Mint-Yogurt Dip or a sweet and tangy mango chutney.
Often enjoyed as a shared snack or appetizer.
instructions: Cook basmati rice according to package directions. Cool completely.
Boil or steam potatoes until tender. Peel and mash well.
Heat 15 ml of vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté minced red onion until translucent.
Add grated ginger and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in mild curry powder. Cook for 30 seconds, blooming the spices.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, mashed potatoes, sautéed aromatics, finely diced green apple, chopped fresh coriander, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Form the mixture into small, cylindrical croquettes, about 5 cm long and 2 cm thick.
Prepare three shallow dishes: one with plain flour, one with beaten egg, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each croquette in flour, tap off excess. Dip in beaten egg, then coat completely with breadcrumbs.
Heat 200 ml vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Shallow fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Drain fried croquettes on paper towels.
Serve warm with Mint-Yogurt Dip.
notes: Ensure rice and potatoes are completely cool before mixing to help with forming.
For a healthier option, croquettes can be baked at 200°C (390°F) for 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Vegetable & Parmesan Bake with Pickled Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of the layered vegetable bake stands proudly on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate. The top crust is a rich golden-brown from melted parmesan cheese. Beneath, clearly visible layers of soft, deep purple eggplant, tender white potato, and vibrant red tomato are arranged neatly. The vegetables show a slight caramelization on their edges from baking. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adds a pop of color. Bright pink, thinly sliced quick-pickled red onions are artfully placed on top and around the bake, providing a sharp visual contrast and highlighting the fermentation element. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is folded simply beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green foliage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread.
A simple green salad.
instructions: Thinly slice red onions. Combine with red wine vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl. Let marinate for at least 30 minutes to quick-pickle.
Slice eggplants, potatoes, and tomatoes into 5mm thick rounds. Dice yellow onion and mince garlic.
Lightly salt eggplant slices. Let sit for 15 minutes. Pat dry with a paper towel.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear eggplant slices in batches until lightly golden on both sides. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
In the same pan, add 20ml olive oil. Sauté diced yellow onion and minced garlic over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in dried oregano. Remove from heat.
Lightly grease a 20x30cm baking dish with olive oil.
Arrange a layer of potato slices at the bottom of the dish. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread half of the sautéed onion and garlic mixture over the potatoes.
Layer half of the seared eggplant slices over the onions.
Arrange half of the tomato slices over the eggplant. Season lightly.
Repeat layers with remaining potato, onion mixture, eggplant, and tomato slices. Drizzle remaining 50ml olive oil over the top.
Cover the baking dish with foil. Bake for 40 minutes.
Remove foil. Continue baking for 20-25 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese evenly over the top. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is golden brown and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and the quick-pickled red onions.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing full vegetables and quick-pickling onions as a preservation method.

recipes.recipe_name: Baharat-Crusted Shrimp with Coconut Kudzu Polenta and Hibiscus-Chocolate Reduction
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, free-form dollop of creamy, off-white coconut kudzu polenta forms the base, its surface smooth. Nestled beside the polenta are four to five large, plump shrimp. Each shrimp boasts a golden-brown, subtly spiced baharat-breadcrumb crust from searing. The shrimp are arranged organically, showcasing their natural curve as whole pieces. A glossy, deep reddish-brown hibiscus-chocolate reduction is artfully drizzled over both the shrimp and the polenta, creating streaks of rich color and shine. Scattered over the dish is a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. A bright green lime wedge rests on the rim of the plate. The overall presentation is professional yet approachable, with a balance of textures and colors, moderate negative space, and a focus on the quality of ingredients. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table surface and a cotton napkin placed beside the plate, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Prepare Hibiscus-Chocolate Reduction: In a small saucepan, combine hibiscus tea, minced shallot, and minced garlic. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half. Remove from heat. Stir in chopped dark chocolate and 15g butter until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Coconut Kudzu Polenta: In a medium saucepan, bring coconut cream and water/broth to a simmer. Slowly whisk in polenta. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 5-7 minutes. In a small bowl, dissolve kudzu starch in 30ml cold water to create a slurry. Stir kudzu slurry into polenta. Cook for 1 minute more until very thick and creamy. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Prepare Shrimp: Pat shrimp dry with paper towels. In a shallow dish, combine baharat and panko breadcrumbs. Toss shrimp in mixture to coat evenly.

Cook Shrimp: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add breadcrumb-coated shrimp in a single layer. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.

Plate: Spoon warm coconut kudzu polenta onto each plate. Arrange cooked shrimp next to the polenta. Drizzle hibiscus-chocolate reduction over the shrimp and polenta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Portobello Mushrooms with Feta and Rosemary
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted portobello mushroom is the centerpiece, presented gill-side up on a clean white round porcelain plate. The mushroom cap is a rich, dark brown, showcasing a tender, succulent texture. It is generously filled with a golden-brown feta and rosemary crumble, which appears slightly crisp and textured on top. Around the mushroom, a scattering of vibrant red cherry tomatoes, roasted until their skins are slightly blistered and softened, provides a burst of color. A delicate sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a final touch of freshness. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wipe portobello mushrooms clean with a damp cloth. Gently remove the stems.
In a small bowl, combine 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, and half of the chopped rosemary.
Brush the inside (gill-side) of each mushroom cap generously with the oil mixture. Season with salt and black pepper.
Place mushrooms, gill-side up, on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes.
While mushrooms roast, prepare the feta crumble. In another bowl, combine crumbled feta, breadcrumbs, remaining chopped rosemary, and 15ml olive oil. Mix well until combined.
Remove mushrooms from the oven. Fill each roasted mushroom cap with the feta-breadcrumb mixture.
Arrange cherry tomatoes on the baking sheet around the mushrooms.
Return to the oven. Roast for an additional 10-12 minutes, or until the feta crumble is golden brown and the mushrooms are tender.
Garnish immediately with fresh chopped parsley. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Carrot Avgolemono Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Tomato & Carrot Avgolemono Soup is presented in a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic bowl, showcasing a pale yellow, creamy broth. Visible within are tender grains of rice, small, irregular chunks of vibrant orange fermented carrots, and reddish fermented tomatoes. The soup is garnished with delicate sprigs of fresh green dill and a swirl of golden extra virgin olive oil. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin and a traditional Greek olive wood spoon are placed beside it. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the natural colors and textures of the dish to be the focal point, emphasizing the dish's sustainable and rustic Greek essence. The entire bowl is visible, with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Prepare zero-waste chicken stock. Simmer chicken bones, onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends, bay leaf, peppercorns in water for 3-4 hours. Strain stock.
In a large pot, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté finely diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add 100g short-grain rice to the pot. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in 1.5 litres strained chicken stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes, until rice is tender.
Drain 150g fermented carrots and 150g fermented tomatoes. Add to the soup. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Prepare avgolemono: In a separate bowl, whisk 3 eggs until frothy. Slowly add 100ml fresh lemon juice, whisking constantly.
Temper avgolemono: Slowly ladle 2-3 cups of hot soup broth into the egg-lemon mixture, whisking continuously.
Pour tempered avgolemono mixture back into the pot, stirring constantly. Do not boil after adding avgolemono. Heat gently until the soup slightly thickens.
Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in 15ml olive oil.
Ladle soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh dill sprigs. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Tagliatelle with Cultured Ricotta, Fermented Spinach & Sun-dried Tomato Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sustainable Tagliatelle is presented in a deep, handcrafted ceramic bowl with an organic, matte cream finish. The tagliatelle, cooked al dente, forms a neat, elevated nest in the center of the bowl, its golden strands lightly coated with a vibrant green hue from the fresh and fermented spinach. Bright green pieces of lacto-fermented spinach are visibly interspersed throughout the pasta, offering a textural contrast. On top, a generous, creamy dollop of bright white cultured ricotta cheese sits elegantly, slightly off-center. Scattered around the ricotta and over the pasta are golden-brown, irregular chunks of crispy sourdough crumble, providing a rustic texture. Small, vivid crimson pieces of finely minced sun-dried tomato are sprinkled over the dish, adding concentrated color. A delicate drizzle of golden olive oil glistens on the surface. The background is a clean, light-toned reclaimed wood table, with an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige folded loosely to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a minimalist, unfussy backdrop.
instructions: Prepare fermented spinach: Roughly chop 100g of spinach. Place in a clean jar. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt. Massage spinach. Cover with filtered water. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days. Refrigerate once tangy.

Prepare sourdough crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. Tear stale sourdough bread into small pieces. Toss with 15ml olive oil, pinch of salt, and pepper. Bake for 10-12 minutes until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Prepare sun-dried tomato topping: Drain sun-dried tomatoes, reserving the oil from the jar. Finely mince the drained tomatoes. Set aside.
Prepare cultured ricotta: In a bowl, whisk ricotta with kefir or buttermilk until smooth. Season with a pinch of salt. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Cook remaining spinach: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add finely minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute. Add remaining 200g fresh spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add tagliatelle. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

Assemble dish: Drain pasta, reserving 60ml pasta water. Return pasta to pot. Add cooked fresh spinach and fermented spinach (drained). Add 30ml of the reserved sun-dried tomato oil from the jar and a squeeze of lemon juice. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water as needed for a light sauce.

Serve immediately. Divide pasta among four bowls. Top each serving with a generous spoonful of cultured ricotta. Sprinkle with sourdough crumble and the minced sun-dried tomato topping. Finish with a drizzle of fresh olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken & Macaroni Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Chicken & Macaroni Potato Gratin is presented as a single, generous portion in a clean, white porcelain ramekin, placed on a simple white dinner plate. The top crust is a rich golden-brown, showcasing crispy panko breadcrumbs and tender, thinly sliced potatoes. Beneath the crust, the creamy, bubbly cheese sauce with al dente elbow macaroni and succulent chicken chunks is visible at the edges. Hints of red chili add subtle color contrast. A light sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface with natural, even lighting. A clean cotton napkin and standard flatware are placed beside the plate, creating a professional yet approachable bistro setting. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, highlighting texture and warmth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Lightly grease a 20x30 cm baking dish or four individual gratin dishes.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.

Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken and set aside. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) during baking.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, diced red chili, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour and cook for 2 minutes, creating a roux.

Gradually whisk in warm milk and chicken stock until smooth and thickened. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add seared chicken chunks and cooked macaroni to the cheese sauce. Stir to combine.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish(es). Arrange thinly sliced potatoes evenly over the top. Sprinkle panko breadcrumbs over the potatoes.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the gratin is bubbly and the potato topping is golden brown and crispy. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Garlic Macaroni and Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp crust, is the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it rests a creamy mound of garlic macaroni, glossy and flecked with finely diced onion and minced garlic. Golden-brown, 2cm potato cubes are artfully arranged next to the chicken, showing their crispy exterior. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted herb breadcrumbs over the chicken and macaroni, adding texture and a hint of fresh parsley. A small sprig of fresh parsley provides a touch of vibrant green. The plating is organized yet natural, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, with silver flatware and a light grey cotton napkin placed beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting for a modern bistro feel.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 400g (e.g., Maris Piper or Russet), cut into 2cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and fresh thyme leaves. Roast for 25-30 minutes until golden and crispy.
Pulse bread slices in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Toss with 15ml olive oil and 10g chopped parsley. Set aside.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan and rest for 5 minutes.
In the same pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Add cooked macaroni. Toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
In a small dry pan, toast the prepared breadcrumbs over medium heat until golden and crisp.

To plate, place a portion of garlic macaroni on a white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange a pan-seared chicken breast beside it. Spoon crispy potatoes next to the chicken. Sprinkle toasted herb breadcrumbs over the chicken and macaroni. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Forest Mushroom Velouté
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Forest Mushroom Velouté is presented in a classic, clean white porcelain soup bowl. The soup is a rich, warm, earthy brown color, smooth and velvety in texture. Centered on the soup, a small, artfully arranged cluster of golden-brown sautéed mushroom slices, thinly sliced, provides a textural contrast. A delicate sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley or chives, along with a few fresh thyme leaves, adds vibrant green color and freshness. An optional subtle drizzle of truffle oil forms a faint swirl on the surface. The bowl is placed on a simple, light-toned wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver soup spoon are positioned neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's inviting warmth and the garnishes' freshness. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the elegantly presented dish.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley or chives, finely chopped

instructions: Place dried porcini mushrooms in a small bowl. Cover with 150 ml hot water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve; reserve liquid. Chop rehydrated porcini.
Clean fresh mushrooms. Slice 100 g thinly for garnish. Roughly chop remaining 400 g.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped fresh mushrooms and chopped rehydrated porcini. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms release their liquid and start to brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Pour in reserved porcini liquid and vegetable stock. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Simmer for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

Remove thyme sprigs. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup until very smooth. Alternatively, blend in batches in a regular blender. Strain soup through a fine-mesh sieve for an extra smooth texture, if desired.
Return soup to the pot. Stir in heavy cream. Heat gently, do not boil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
In a small pan, melt remaining 15 g butter over medium-high heat. Add thinly sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 3-4 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry (Pad Kra Pao Gai)
recipes.visual_description: A single, homely portion of Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate. A generous mound of fluffy white jasmine rice occupies one side of the plate. Next to it, the stir-fry of diced chicken, vibrant green beans, and dark green holy basil is spooned, slightly overlapping the rice. The chicken cubes are cooked to a golden-brown with caramelized edges, coated in a glossy, dark brown savory sauce. Thin slices of bright red chilies are visible throughout the stir-fry. A single, perfectly fried egg with a crispy, golden-brown edge and a bright, runny yellow yolk rests on top of the stir-fry. The arrangement is casual and natural, filling the plate adequately without overcrowding. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A traditional Thai spoon and fork are placed beside the plate. A small, simple ceramic bowl containing Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies) sits nearby, along with a casually placed cloth napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Serve with a crispy fried egg (kai dao) on top.
Offer Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies) on the side for added spice and seasoning.
Eat with a spoon and fork, a common Thai dining practice.

ingredients.name: Green beans
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, trimmed, cut into 2 cm pieces

instructions: Combine fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and water in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves. This is the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced chicken. Stir-fry, breaking up any clumps, until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add green beans. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Pour in the prepared sauce. Stir well to coat chicken and vegetables. Cook for 1 minute until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in holy basil leaves until just wilted.
In a separate pan, heat a little oil. Fry 4 eggs until whites are crispy and yolks are still runny.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice, topped with a fried egg.
notes: Authentic holy basil (Grapao) is crucial for the traditional flavor profile of this dish. Thai basil can be used as a substitute if holy basil is unavailable.
Adjust the quantity of Thai red chilies according to your preferred spice level.
A crispy fried egg with a runny yolk is a classic and highly recommended accompaniment to Pad Kra Pao Gai.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Mashed Potatoes and Gravy
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of crispy pan-seared chicken thigh rests on a bed of creamy mashed potatoes. The chicken skin is deep golden brown and visibly crisp, with natural textures. The meat is juicy and appears as a whole piece. Mashed potatoes are generously spooned, forming a soft mound. A rich, dark brown gravy is poured over a portion of the chicken and cascades down the mashed potatoes, creating natural pools. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the dish as a simple, functional garnish. The plate is an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate with subtle imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple linen napkin is casually folded beside the plate, with a standard fork and knife. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a comfortable family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add fresh thyme sprigs. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F).
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside to rest.
While chicken roasts, boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes. Return to pot. Mash with 50g butter and warm milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
To make gravy, place skillet (with drippings) over medium heat. Remove thyme sprigs.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, scraping up browned bits.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until gravy thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve crispy chicken thighs with mashed potatoes and gravy.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Plum & Lotus Seed Mini Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine mini entremet sits centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a muted cream tone, showcasing the dish's minimalist elegance. The entremet is a clean-edged cylinder, approximately 6 cm in diameter and 4 cm high, with distinct visible layers. The base is a pale, slightly translucent glutinous rice cake, topped by a dense, light brown layer of lotus seed paste. Above this, a vibrant ruby-red square of fermented plum gelée is visible, subtly contrasting with the creamy white vanilla evaporated milk mousse that forms the top layer. The mousse has a smooth, matte finish. A single small purple viola edible flower is delicately placed off-center on the mousse. The plate is set on a light, textured bamboo surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural foliage subtly blurred.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a light, elegant dessert after a meal.
instructions: Prepare Lotus Seed Paste: Soak lotus seeds overnight. Drain. Boil seeds until tender, about 30 minutes. Drain. Blend seeds with 50g sugar and 100ml water until smooth. Pass through a sieve. Cook paste in a non-stick pan over medium heat until thick and dry, about 10-15 minutes. Cool completely.

Prepare Fermented Plum Gelée: Dice fresh plums. Combine diced plums with maesil-cheong and 100ml water in a saucepan. Simmer 10 minutes until plums soften. Dissolve agar-agar in a small amount of cold water, then add to plum mixture. Stir constantly for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish to a thickness of 0.5 cm. Chill until set. Cut into 3 cm squares.

Prepare Glutinous Rice Cake Base: Combine glutinous rice flour and 80ml hot water in a bowl. Mix until a dough forms. Knead briefly until smooth. Roll dough to 0.5 cm thick. Cut into 4 cm rounds. Steam rice cakes for 8-10 minutes until translucent and chewy. Cool.

Prepare Vanilla Evaporated Milk Mousse: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. Gently heat evaporated milk in a small saucepan until warm. Do not boil. Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into warm milk until dissolved. Add vanilla extract. Chill mixture until slightly thickened but still pourable, about 30-40 minutes.

Assemble Mini Entremets: Line 4 individual ring molds (6 cm diameter) with acetate. Place one steamed rice cake round at the bottom of each mold. Top with a layer of lotus seed paste, spreading evenly. Place a plum gelée square on top of the lotus seed paste. Pour the chilled vanilla evaporated milk mousse over the gelée, filling the mold to the top. Gently tap molds to release air bubbles. Chill for at least 4 hours, or until fully set.
Demold and Serve: Carefully remove entremets from molds. Peel off acetate. Garnish each entremet with a single edible flower.
notes: For a truly zero-waste approach, save plum pits and simmer them with a little water to create a subtle plum-infused syrup for other uses.
Maesil-cheong (Korean plum syrup) is key for authentic fermented plum flavor. It can be found in Korean grocery stores.

recipes.recipe_name: Salmon & Dill Cakes with Sourdough Crumb Crust
recipes.visual_description: A single serving is presented on a round, handcrafted cream ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, pan-seared salmon and dill cakes, 7 cm diameter, 2 cm thick, are slightly off-center. Their exterior is a rich, craggy texture from toasted sourdough crumbs, contrasting with soft, flaked salmon. Alongside, a neat bundle of vibrant green, blanched asparagus spears (8-10 cm lengths) is arranged. A small, mounded pile of translucent, pale orange fermented carrot ribbons, curled and delicate, provides a subtle pop of color. Ample white space highlights pure forms and natural colors. The minimalist, eco-conscious setting features the plate on a light reclaimed wood surface. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing organic textures. The background is clean, with subtle natural elements.

ingredients.name: stale sourdough bread, processed into coarse crumbs

instructions: Prepare Fermented Carrots (can be done days in advance): Slice carrots into thin ribbons using a peeler. Dissolve 5g salt in 250ml filtered water to make brine. Pack carrot ribbons and dill sprigs tightly into a clean jar. Pour brine over carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.

Prepare Salmon Mixture: Preheat oven to 180°C. Bake salmon fillet for 12-15 minutes until just cooked through. Let cool slightly. Flake salmon into a large bowl, removing any bones. Add chopped fresh dill, egg, 5g salt, and 2g pepper. Mix gently until combined.
Form Salmon Cakes: Divide salmon mixture into 8 equal portions. Form each portion into a compact, round cake, about 2 cm thick.

Coat Cakes: Place flour in a shallow dish. Place sourdough breadcrumbs in another shallow dish. Dredge each salmon cake in flour, shaking off excess. Then press firmly into sourdough breadcrumbs to coat completely on all sides.

Cook Salmon Cakes: Heat 30ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add 4 salmon cakes. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Remove and keep warm. Repeat with remaining oil and cakes.

Cook Seasonal Vegetables: While cakes cook, blanch asparagus. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add asparagus. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and refresh in ice water to retain color. Drain well.
Plate Dish: Place two salmon cakes on each plate. Arrange a small portion of blanched asparagus alongside. Garnish with a small mound of fermented carrot ribbons.
notes: This recipe emphasizes reducing food waste by using stale sourdough bread for crumbs and incorporates fermentation for flavor and preservation. Sourcing local, seasonal produce is encouraged.

recipes.recipe_name: Dill & Lemon Crusted Salmon
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of baked Dill & Lemon Crusted Salmon is centrally placed on a round, simple ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The salmon fillet is presented whole, its golden-brown, textured crust of breadcrumbs and green dill flakes is prominent. The salmon itself is a warm, cooked pink. To the side, a small, natural cluster of bright green steamed asparagus spears rests, not overly arranged. A small lemon wedge is placed beside the salmon. The plate sits on a light-colored, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded, plain linen napkin in a neutral tone lies next to the plate. Standard, well-worn silver cutlery is present. The background is a soft, out-of-focus view of a cozy, lived-in home kitchen, with warm, inviting lighting. The overall scene is natural, unpretentious, and comforting, showcasing the dish as a homely, satisfying meal.

ingredients.name: Salmon fillets, skin on or off

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, combine Panko breadcrumbs, chopped fresh dill, lemon zest from the whole lemon, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder. Mix well.
Brush each salmon fillet lightly with olive oil.
Press the breadcrumb mixture firmly onto the top side of each salmon fillet. Ensure a thick, even crust.
Place crusted salmon fillets on the prepared baking tray.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C and crust is golden and crisp. Cooking time varies with fillet thickness.
Remove from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice from half of the lemon over each cooked fillet before serving.
notes: Serve immediately with your favorite simple side, such as steamed vegetables or a light green salad.
Adjust baking time based on the thickness of your salmon fillets. Thicker fillets may require a few more minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso Glazed Shrimp and Tofu Donburi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Miso Glazed Shrimp and Tofu Donburi is presented in a deep, dark ceramic donburi bowl. Steamed Japanese short-grain rice forms the base. Arranged neatly on top are golden-brown, seared 2cm tofu cubes and plump, pink-orange glazed shrimp. The miso glaze coats the shrimp and tofu, creating a glossy, rich surface. Vibrant green rehydrated wakame seaweed is placed alongside. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green spring onions and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space around the central ingredients. The colors are natural and appealing, showcasing the freshness of the ingredients. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a pair of dark wooden chopsticks and a small white ceramic dish containing light pink pickled ginger (gari) for an authentic Japanese dining experience. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
Offer a small side dish of pickled ginger (gari) or tsukemono (Japanese pickles).
A small bowl of clear dashi soup can accompany the meal.
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook according to package directions. Keep warm.
Rehydrate wakame seaweed in cold water for 10 minutes. Drain well. Gently squeeze out excess water.
Cut pressed tofu into 2cm cubes.
Pat shrimp very dry with paper towels.
In a small bowl, whisk together white miso paste, mirin, sake, soy sauce, sugar, and water for the glaze.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes to the pan. Sear until golden brown and slightly crisp on all sides, about 6-8 minutes. Remove tofu from pan. Set aside.
Add shrimp to the same pan. Cook for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and almost cooked through.
Return seared tofu to the pan with the shrimp. Pour half of the prepared miso glaze over the shrimp and tofu.
Toss gently to coat all ingredients. Cook for 1-2 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and adhere. Ensure shrimp internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Divide cooked rice among 4 individual donburi bowls.
Arrange the glazed shrimp and tofu mixture over the rice in each bowl.
Place a portion of rehydrated wakame seaweed alongside the main ingredients.
Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake sits on a matte cream ceramic plate. The dish consists of oven-roasted, golden-brown potato cubes and seared chicken chunks arranged in a natural, overlapping heap. Melted sharp cheddar cheese drapes over the components, showing bubbly textures and toasted edges. Vibrant green chopped chives are sprinkled evenly over the cheese. The arrangement is asymmetrical and casual, filling the center of the plate while leaving clean margins. The plate rests on a dark, textured wooden table next to a stainless steel fork and a neutral linen napkin. Warm, directional kitchen lighting enhances the crispy potato skins and the glossy, melted cheese. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sour cream
Pair with a fresh green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Toss potatoes with 15ml oil, half the salt, and half the paprika.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Season chicken with remaining oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and pepper.
Add chicken to the baking sheet with potatoes.
Roast for 15 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar over the chicken and potatoes.
Bake 3 minutes until cheese melts and bubbles.
Garnish with finely chopped chives.
notes: Cut potatoes into uniform cubes to ensure even roasting
Use sharp cheddar for the best flavor profile
Ensure chicken chunks are not touching to allow browning

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce and Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A crispy-skinned, pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown, rests slightly off-center on a round white porcelain dinner plate. Roasted new potatoes, halved, with golden-brown, slightly charred edges, are clustered naturally beside the chicken. A creamy mushroom sauce, featuring visible sliced cremini mushrooms, halved vibrant red cherry tomatoes, and bright yellow corn kernels, is generously spooned over the chicken and potatoes, pooling invitingly around them. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a pop of green. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures. The background is a soft, blurred modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompanied by a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden-brown. Flip chicken.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

While chicken roasts, toss potatoes with remaining 15ml olive oil, 2 cloves minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast in the same oven for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and golden-brown.
Remove chicken from pan, set aside. Drain excess fat, leaving 15ml in the pan. Melt butter in the pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and remaining 2 cloves minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Stir in Dijon mustard and chopped oregano. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Reduce by half, about 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream, halved cherry tomatoes, and corn kernels. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken thighs with roasted potatoes. Spoon creamy mushroom sauce generously over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang-Doenjang Turkey & Beef Jjim
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Gochujang-Doenjang Turkey & Beef Jjim is presented in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl with a subtly textured, matte finish. The bowl is filled with generous, dark reddish-brown chunks of tender braised turkey and beef, nestled among soft, thick rounds of daikon radish, vibrant orange oblique-cut carrots, and plump, halved shiitake mushrooms. A rich, glossy, gochujang-doenjang sauce coats all ingredients. The dish is sparingly garnished with a scattering of thinly sliced diagonal green onions and a few delicate slivers of fresh red chili, providing contrasting color and freshness. To the side of the main bowl, a small, matching ceramic dish holds a neat mound of quick-fermented kkakdugi, showcasing small, crisp, chili-dusted daikon cubes. The overall plating is minimalistic, allowing natural ingredient colors and textures to dominate. The setting features a light, natural bamboo table surface. Metal chopsticks rest beside the bowl, with a simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, with a clean, minimalist background that includes subtle hints of green plants, emphasizing a connection to nature and sustainable practices.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly steamed short-grain white rice.
Offer with other traditional banchan (small side dishes) like seasoned spinach or bean sprouts.
Provide a small spoon for the sauce and a pair of metal chopsticks.

ingredients.name: Daikon radish
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, peeled and cut into 2 cm thick rounds

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into oblique chunks

ingredients.name: Shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.quantity: 150 g, stems removed, halved if large

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.quantity: 2 stalks, thinly sliced diagonally for garnish

ingredients.name: Small daikon radish
ingredients.quantity: 200 g, for quick kkakdugi (cut into 1.5 cm cubes)

instructions: Pat turkey and beef chunks dry.
In a large bowl, combine gochujang, doenjang, minced garlic (6 cloves), soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, brown sugar, and black pepper. Mix well.
Add turkey and beef chunks to the marinade. Toss to coat thoroughly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add a splash of neutral oil.
Sear marinated turkey and beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove meat and set aside.
Add quartered onion and remaining 2 cloves minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Return seared meat to the pot. Add daikon rounds, carrots, and shiitake mushrooms.
Pour in beef or vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 60-90 minutes, or until meat is very tender. Stir occasionally. Ensure turkey reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
While jjim braises, prepare quick kkakdugi. In a separate bowl, combine cubed daikon radish, salt, sugar, rice vinegar, minced garlic, and gochugaru. Mix well. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Taste the jjim and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with sliced green onions and fresh red chili if desired. Serve quick kkakdugi alongside.
traditional_techniques: Fermentation (inherent in Gochujang and Doenjang, and applied to quick Kkakdugi)

recipes.recipe_name: Ebi Tofu Tomato Donburi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Ebi Tofu Tomato Donburi is presented in a clean white porcelain donburi bowl, showcasing a harmonious composition. The base is fluffy white short-grain rice. On top, whole reddish-pink seared shrimp are nestled alongside golden-brown, 2 cm seared tofu cubes and vibrant red tomato wedges. A glossy, light brown savory sauce lightly coats the ingredients. Thinly sliced bright green scallions are scattered over the dish, adding a fresh color contrast and visual texture. The bowl is placed on a simple light wooden table. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a small ceramic chopstick rest beside the bowl. A folded neutral-colored cotton napkin is positioned neatly. Natural, even overhead lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual, contemporary Japanese eatery.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook 600g rice according to package directions.
Peel and devein 400g shrimp. Pat dry.
Drain 400g firm tofu. Press excess water. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Cut 300g tomatoes into 8 wedges each.
Thinly slice 3 stalks green onions. Mince 20g ginger and 2 cloves garlic.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove tofu.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add minced ginger and garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the pan. Cook 1-2 minutes until just turning pink.
Add tomato wedges. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in 200ml dashi, 60ml soy sauce, 30ml mirin, 30ml sake, and 15g sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared tofu to the pan. Simmer 3-5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Do not overcook shrimp.
Divide cooked rice among 4 donburi bowls.
Spoon shrimp, tofu, and tomato mixture over the rice. Include some sauce.
Garnish with sliced green onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tempura Shrimp and Tofu with Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tempura Shrimp and Tofu is artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Four golden-brown, crispy tempura shrimp, tails intact, are positioned diagonally. Beside them, four irregular, craggy pieces of lightly fried tempura tofu sit, exhibiting a delicate crisp exterior. A mound of perfectly steamed, fluffy white Japanese short-grain rice occupies one side. A small, elegant ceramic bowl holds the clear amber tentsuyu dipping sauce. Adjacent to the sauce, small mounds of finely grated daikon radish and freshly grated ginger are presented. The presentation is clean, balanced, and minimalist, with ample negative space. A simple wooden table, folded linen napkin, and dark wooden chopsticks beside a traditional rice bowl complete the modern Japanese bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup.
Offer small bowls of pickled vegetables (tsukemono).
Provide individual rice bowls and chopsticks for each diner.
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Peel and devein shrimp, leaving tails on. Make small slits on the underside of each shrimp to prevent curling. Pat dry.
Drain tofu. Cut tofu block into 8 equal rectangular chunks. Gently pat dry with paper towels.
For tentsuyu sauce, combine dashi stock, soy sauce, and mirin in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Remove from heat. Keep warm.
Grate daikon radish and fresh ginger. Set aside for garnish.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or wok to 170°C (340°F).
In a large bowl, whisk tempura flour and ice water until just combined. Do not overmix; lumps are fine.

Dip each shrimp into the tempura batter, allowing excess to drip off. Fry shrimp in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and crisp. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack.
Dip each tofu chunk into the tempura batter. Fry tofu in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden and crisp. Remove and drain on a wire rack.
Serve tempura shrimp and tofu immediately with steamed rice, tentsuyu dipping sauce, grated daikon, and grated ginger.
notes: Keep tempura batter very cold by placing the bowl over an ice bath while frying.
Do not overmix the batter; lumps create a crispier texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Beef & Mushroom Doenjang Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean Beef & Mushroom Doenjang Soup is presented in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed rim. The rich, savory broth, a deep golden-brown, holds tender, irregular chunks of braised beef and delicate, thin slices of rehydrated shiitake mushrooms. A vibrant scattering of thinly sliced green onions rests on the surface, offering a fresh green contrast. Alongside, a small, vibrant mound of fermented red kimchi adds a pop of color and texture. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the bowl on a light-colored, textured stone surface. The background is softly blurred, hinting at natural elements like a subtle plant, under soft, natural lighting. Simple, traditional Korean chopsticks rest beside the bowl on an undyed linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of freshly cooked white rice.
Offer additional kimchi and other banchan (small side dishes) on the side.
Serve with a metal spoon for the broth and chopsticks for the solids.
instructions: Soak dried shiitake mushrooms in 500 ml warm water for 30 minutes. Reserve mushroom soaking liquid.
Cut beef into 3-4 cm chunks.
In a large pot, combine beef, beef stock, cheddar cheese rinds, and reserved mushroom soaking liquid. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours, skimming any foam.
Remove cheddar rinds from the pot. Discard rinds.
Squeeze excess water from rehydrated shiitake mushrooms. Remove stems. Slice mushroom caps thinly.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms and minced garlic to the pot. Continue to simmer for another 30 minutes, until beef is tender.
In a small bowl, whisk doenjang with a ladleful of hot broth until smooth. Stir the mixture back into the soup.
Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and a dollop of kimchi.
Serve hot.
notes: This recipe utilizes cheddar cheese rinds, a zero-waste technique, to add subtle umami to the broth without overpowering the traditional Korean flavors.
The mushroom soaking liquid is incorporated into the broth for extra depth and umami, minimizing waste.
Doenjang, a fermented soybean paste, is a cornerstone of Korean cuisine and provides a rich, complex flavor profile to the soup.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Date & Lotus Seed Gangjeong with Umami Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic arrangement of three to four irregular, earth-toned gangjeong pieces rests on a handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate. Each piece, roughly 2x2 cm, exhibits a slightly puffed, uneven surface, coated in a deep reddish-brown glaze from the red date and malt syrup, subtly revealing pale specks of lotus seed. The gangjeong pieces are artfully scattered, not in a rigid pattern, allowing for ample negative space on the plate. A delicate scattering of dark, glistening umami crisp, made from finely crushed candied anchovies, garnishes the gangjeong, adding a surprising textural and flavor contrast. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A small, simple Korean tea bowl with a subtle pattern and a single, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue complete the serene, eco-conscious setting. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and natural colors of the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of traditional Korean tea, such as Sujeonggwa (cinnamon punch) or barley tea.
Enjoy as a light dessert after a meal or with a tea ceremony.
instructions: Soak pitted red dates in hot water for 30 minutes until softened. Drain. Combine dates, 100ml water, 20g malt syrup, and salt in a blender. Blend until smooth paste forms. Set aside.
Rinse lotus seeds. Combine lotus seeds and 200ml water in a small pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 20-30 minutes. Drain and mash into a coarse paste.
In a bowl, combine glutinous rice flour and 5g sesame oil. Gradually add hot water, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. Knead lightly for 2 minutes.
Roll dough into a thin sheet, about 0.5 cm thick. Cut into small, irregular squares or rectangles, approximately 2x2 cm.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Lightly pan-fry dough pieces until puffed and lightly golden, turning occasionally.

In a small dry pan, gently toast small dried anchovies until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Remove and cool. Crush anchovies very finely using a mortar and pestle or a small food processor. Return crushed anchovies to pan. Add sugar and 5ml sesame oil. Stir over low heat until sugar melts and coats anchovies, creating a slightly sticky, candied crisp. Spread on parchment paper to cool and harden.
In a small saucepan, combine 100g malt syrup and 30ml water. Heat gently until syrup is fluid and warm.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked gangjeong pieces with the red date paste and lotus seed paste. Mix gently until evenly coated.
Pour the warm malt syrup coating over the gangjeong mixture. Gently toss to coat all pieces thoroughly.
Spread coated gangjeong pieces onto a sheet of parchment paper. Let cool slightly until firm enough to handle. Arrange individual portions on serving plates. Sprinkle generously with the Umami Crisp.
notes: The 'fermented' aspect of the red date paste here is more about creating a rich, complex flavor through a prolonged soak and gentle cooking, akin to traditional preserves. For a true fermentation, dates would be submerged in brine or a starter for an extended period.
The small dried anchovies (myeolchi) are a common Korean pantry item and, when candied, provide a unique sweet-savory counterpoint, a characteristic often found in Korean cuisine.
traditional_techniques: Using Jocheong (malt syrup) as a primary sweetener
Preparation of Gangjeong, a traditional Korean confectionery
The sweet-savory balance, characteristic of many Korean dishes

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano with Roasted Corn and Mustard Greens Salad
recipes.visual_description: A rich, dark Mole Poblano sauce forms a glossy pool on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Resting centrally on the mole is a perfectly pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening under the sauce, presented whole. To one side, a small, vibrant mound of crisp mustard greens salad, lightly dressed, adds a fresh, contrasting green. Adjacent, roasted corn kernels, some with subtle charring, provide pops of yellow. The plate is clean, with moderate negative space. Toasted sesame seeds are sprinkled over the chicken and mole. A warm, folded corn tortilla rests beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, natural even lighting, with a cotton napkin placed neatly.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
instructions: Prepare Dried Chilies: Remove stems and seeds from ancho, guajillo, and chipotle chilies. Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Toast chilies for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Transfer to a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let soak for 20-30 minutes until softened. Drain, reserving some soaking liquid.
Toast Nuts and Seeds: In the same dry pan, toast almonds, pumpkin seeds, and half of the sesame seeds separately until lightly golden and fragrant. Set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add chopped tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.

Blend Mole Base: In a blender, combine softened chilies, sautéed onion, garlic, tomatoes, toasted almonds, pumpkin seeds, half of the toasted sesame seeds, torn tortilla, and torn bread. Add 250 ml hot chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. Add more broth if needed to aid blending.

Cook Mole Sauce: Strain the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into the large pot or Dutch oven, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Add remaining chicken broth to the strained sauce. Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Stir in chocolate, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, cinnamon, cloves, cumin, and oregano. Simmer for at least 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and flavors meld. Season with salt. The mole should be rich and dark.
Roast Corn: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss corn kernels with 5 ml olive oil and salt. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and slightly charred.

Cook Chicken: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Let rest for 5 minutes.

Prepare Salad: Whisk together 30 ml olive oil, 15 ml apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, and honey/agave nectar for the vinaigrette. Season with salt and pepper. Toss mustard greens with the vinaigrette just before serving.

Assemble Dish: Spoon a generous amount of mole sauce onto the center of each white porcelain plate. Place a seared chicken thigh on top of the mole. Arrange a portion of roasted corn next to the chicken. Place a small mound of dressed mustard greens salad on the plate.
Garnish: Sprinkle remaining toasted sesame seeds over the mole and chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Duck Breast with Creamed Corn and Chocolate-Mustard Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared duck breast is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The duck, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, is sliced into three thick medallions, arranged neatly at the center. Beside it, a generous dollop of creamy, pale yellow corn purée provides a soft base. A rich, dark brown chocolate-mustard glaze is artfully drizzled over the duck and around the plate, catching the light. A vibrant side salad of fresh mixed greens, lightly dressed, offers a contrasting color and crisp texture. The overall composition is balanced and elegant, showcasing a refined yet approachable meal. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, illuminated by natural, even light, with a folded cotton napkin beside it, evoking a modern bistro ambiance.
