Chill: Pour soup into a large pitcher or bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until thoroughly chilled.
Serve: Ladle chilled gazpacho into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with crumbled feta, a drizzle of olive oil, and a few small mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Creamy Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homestyle Creamy Chicken and Rice is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Diced chicken pieces, approximately 2-3 cm, are cooked until golden and nestled among fluffy, creamy rice, enriched by diced carrots and tender pieces of tomato. The dish has a warm, inviting golden-orange hue from the tomato and coconut milk, with visible specks of green from a light parsley garnish. The texture is soft and comforting, with the rice absorbing the rich, savory sauce. A casual cloth napkin is loosely placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy light emanates from an overhead kitchen fixture, highlighting the dish's comforting appeal. The scene is uncluttered, focusing solely on the hearty, expertly prepared meal.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Dice onion and carrot into small cubes. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Brown on all sides, about 5 minutes. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrot to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and Dijon mustard. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add uncooked rice to the pot. Stir to coat the grains.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return browned chicken to the pot. Stir gently to combine.
Cover the pot, reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and creamy.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Coconut Chicken with Savory Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Coconut Chicken with Savory Tomato Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous bed of fluffy, coconut-infused rice forms the base. Nestled atop are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, coated in a rich, creamy, light orange sauce. The sauce contains finely diced red tomatoes and orange carrots. Vibrant green chopped cilantro or spring onion is lightly scattered over the chicken and sauce. A very light dusting of finely grated hard cheese adds subtle contrast. The dish is arranged naturally, sauce pooling slightly. The plate sits on a simple wooden table with standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a blurred modern bistro background.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3-4 cm chunks
fresh cilantro or spring onion, chopped

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Do not cook through.
In the same pan, add diced onion and carrot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking down tomatoes with a spoon. Pour in chicken broth and 200ml coconut milk. Add Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Stir occasionally.

While chicken simmers, rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed rice, 400ml water, 100ml coconut milk, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Ladle a portion of savory tomato rice onto each plate. Arrange creamy coconut chicken chunks and sauce over the rice. Garnish with grated cheese and fresh cilantro or spring onion.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Liver with Sherry-Porcini Sauce and Apple
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken liver chunks, irregularly shaped, are centrally mounded on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, glossy amber-brown sauce generously pools around the base and lightly coats the liver. Rustic slices of rehydrated porcini mushrooms are interspersed with the liver. Golden-brown apple wedges are artfully arranged beside the liver, adding a contrasting color and texture. Fresh green peppercorns are visible within the sauce. A few small sprigs of fresh thyme are delicately placed on top as garnish. The background is a simple, light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the varied textures. The overall presentation is refined yet inviting, with moderate negative space.

ingredients.name: Apple, firm and tart (e.g., Granny Smith)

instructions: Rehydrate dried porcini mushrooms in 150ml hot water for 20 minutes. Drain mushrooms, reserving liquid. Roughly chop rehydrated porcini.
Pat chicken livers dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Cut each apple into 8-10 rustic wedges. Remove core.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken livers in a single layer. Sear 2-3 minutes per side until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove livers from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced shallots and cook 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and chopped porcini mushrooms. Cook 3 minutes, stirring frequently.
Deglaze skillet with sherry. Scrape up any browned bits. Cook 1 minute until reduced slightly.

Add chicken stock, reserved porcini liquid (strained), Benedictine, green peppercorns, hot chocolate powder, and nutritional yeast. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Stir in fresh thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
While sauce simmers, quickly sauté apple wedges in a separate small pan with a drizzle of olive oil until lightly golden and tender-crisp. About 2-3 minutes.
Return seared chicken livers to the sauce. Gently warm through for 1 minute.
Serve immediately, spooning sauce and mushrooms over chicken livers. Arrange sautéed apple wedges alongside.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Apples with Honey-Walnut Meringue
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm, baked apple rests in a rustic, round ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The apple, unpeeled and slightly softened from baking, is topped with a generous, golden-brown meringue, artfully browned and lightly peaked from baking. Visible within the meringue are small pieces of chopped walnuts, adding texture. The apple’s natural, deep red and yellow skin peeks out from beneath the meringue. A subtle sheen from the honey glaze is present. The setting is a cozy kitchen table, with soft, warm light illuminating the dish. A simple spoon rests beside the bowl, ready for enjoyment. The overall presentation is comforting, inviting, and distinctly homemade, reflecting a satisfying end to a family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Wash and core apples. Do not peel. Leave a small base to hold fillings.
Place apples in a small baking dish. The dish should comfortably hold 4 apples.
Divide 40 ml honey, butter, and cinnamon evenly among apple cavities.
Add 30 ml water to the bottom of the baking dish.
Bake for 25-35 minutes, or until apples are tender but still hold their shape.
While apples bake, prepare meringue.
In a clean, dry bowl, whip egg whites with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form.
Gradually add granulated sugar, whipping until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Gently fold in remaining 20 ml honey and chopped walnuts into the meringue.
Remove apples from oven. Increase oven temperature to 200°C (390°F).
Spoon or pipe meringue mixture over each baked apple, covering the top completely.
Return to oven and bake for 8-12 minutes, or until meringue is golden brown and crisp.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Sausage, Celeriac Purée, Red Wine Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared, golden-brown pork sausage sits slightly off-center on a large, pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent to it, an elegant, natural swipe of creamy, pale ivory celeriac purée creates a fluid, organic shape. A glossy, deep ruby-red red wine jus is artfully drizzled around the sausage and purée, forming delicate, intentional lines that contrast with the plate's abundant negative space. A few vibrant green micro-herbs are precisely placed atop the sausage, adding a touch of fresh color and architectural height. The textures are varied: the crisp exterior of the sausage, the velvety smoothness of the purée, and the subtle sheen of the jus. The presentation is minimalist and refined, showcasing the quality of ingredients and precision of execution on a premium marble surface with a folded white linen napkin and dramatic lighting.
instructions: Prepare Celeriac Purée: Peel celeriac. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, simmer until very tender (15-20 minutes). Drain well. Return to hot pan to dry slightly. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or food mill, or blend with an immersion blender until smooth. Incorporate cream and butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Red Wine Jus: Finely dice shallots and garlic. In a saucepan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Sauté shallots until translucent (3-4 minutes). Add garlic, sauté 1 minute. Pour in red wine. Bring to a simmer, reduce by half. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat, gently simmer until liquid reduces by two-thirds and is syrupy (approx. 20-30 minutes). Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Return jus to clean pan. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Cook Pork Sausage: Heat remaining olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add sausages. Sear on all sides until deeply golden brown (approx. 8-10 minutes total). Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook gently, turning occasionally, until cooked through.

Plate Dish: Place a generous dollop or elegant swipe of celeriac purée on each plate. Place one seared pork sausage next to the purée. Spoon or drizzle red wine jus artfully around the sausage and purée. Garnish with a few microgreens or crispy sage leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Honey-Thyme Apples and Walnuts
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared pork chop, golden brown with a rich crust, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork chop is presented as a whole piece, glistening lightly with sauce. Around it, several golden-hued apple wedges are artfully arranged, some showing slight caramelization. A rich, amber honey-thyme pan sauce pools subtly at the base of the chop and around the apples. Toasted, roughly chopped walnuts are scattered over the apples and sauce, adding textural contrast. Fresh green thyme leaves provide a vibrant color pop. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s textures and warm tones. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted root vegetables or a simple green salad.
Pair with a dry hard cider or a crisp white wine.
instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.

Sear pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove pork chops from skillet, rest on a cutting board.
While pork roasts, core apples. Cut apples into 1 cm thick wedges. No need to peel.
Add butter to the same skillet over medium heat. Add apple wedges and two thyme sprigs. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until apples are tender-crisp and lightly caramelized.
Remove apples from skillet. Set aside. Keep skillet on heat.
Add chicken stock, honey, and apple cider vinegar to the skillet. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce heat and simmer for 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, toast walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant. Roughly chop.
Return pork chops to skillet with sauce for a brief toss. Spoon sauce over pork. Arrange sautéed apple wedges around pork chops.
Garnish with remaining fresh thyme leaves and toasted chopped walnuts. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey Walnut Apple Financiers
recipes.visual_description: Six to eight perfectly uniform, golden-brown financiers are arranged with consistent spacing on a rectangular white porcelain serving platter. Each financier, approximately 7 cm long, displays a slightly crisp exterior and a visible moist, tender crumb flecked with finely diced apple and chopped walnuts. A delicate, translucent honey glaze lightly coats the top, providing a subtle sheen. A single, perfectly toasted walnut half adorns the center of each financier. The overall presentation is clean and elegant, with moderate negative space on the platter. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table, illuminated by soft, even natural light, creating a professional yet inviting atmosphere. A folded white cotton napkin is placed subtly beside the platter, enhancing the restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a cup of coffee or hot tea
Present as part of an assortment of miniature pastries
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and flour 6-8 mini financier molds or mini muffin tins.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until butter browns and smells nutty (beurre noisette). Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove solids. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk together icing sugar, almond flour, plain flour, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg whites with honey until frothy.
Pour egg white mixture into dry ingredients. Fold gently until just combined.
Slowly add cooled browned butter and vanilla extract. Fold until smooth batter forms.
Peel, core, and finely dice the apple into 3 mm cubes. Coarsely chop the 50 g walnuts.
Fold diced apple and chopped walnuts into the batter.
Divide batter evenly among prepared molds. Fill molds about two-thirds full.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, or until financiers are golden brown and spring back when lightly touched.
Remove from oven. Let cool in molds for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze, whisk powdered sugar with water until smooth. Adjust water for desired consistency.
Once financiers are cool, dip tops into the honey glaze. Place a toasted walnut half on top of each glazed financier.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Stout Soup
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rich beef and stout soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The beef is cut into generous 2-3 cm chunks, seared to a deep brown. Carrots are cut into thick 1.5 cm rounds, and potatoes into robust 2.5 cm chunks, all simmered until tender. Diced onion and fennel pieces are visible within the thick, dark, savory broth, which has a slight sheen from the reduced stout. A subtle red hue from the tomatoes peeks through. The soup is garnished simply with fresh, roughly chopped parsley leaves, scattered naturally over the surface. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, alongside a crumpled cloth napkin. The scene is lit by warm, inviting kitchen light, evoking a comforting, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Cut beef into 2-3 cm chunks. Pat dry.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Finely chop chili.
Core and dice fennel bulb. Peel carrots and cut into 1.5 cm rounds. Peel potatoes and cut into 2-3 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, fennel, carrots, garlic, ginger, and chili to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Pour in stout beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer 2 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes, beef stock, maple syrup, and honey to the pot. Stir well.
Return seared beef to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender.
Add potatoes and remaining carrots to the pot. Continue simmering, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in lime juice.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve soup hot, garnished with fresh parsley and thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Reclaimed Harvest Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of 'Reclaimed Harvest Broth' is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy beige tone. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. The broth is crystal clear, a warm golden amber hue, showcasing precisely diced 1 cm cubes of tender orange carrot, pale potato, and translucent white fennel floating gracefully within. A vibrant, reddish-orange dollop of fermented tomato relish rests delicately near the center of the broth, its rich color a striking contrast. A subtle sheen of pale yellow ginger-fennel oil shimmers on the surface. The dish is garnished with a few wispy, bright green fennel fronds. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the clean composition and natural textures. An undyed linen napkin in a matching natural beige is folded neatly beside the bowl. A simple, rustic ceramic spoon is placed nearby. The background is minimal, with a hint of natural plant greenery, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare broth base: Collect carrot peels, potato peels, fennel core and outer layers, ginger peels, garlic skins, and chili stems/seeds. Combine with 1.5 litres beef stock and peppercorns in a large pot. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Set broth aside.

Prepare fermented tomato relish: Dice ripe tomatoes, 2 cloves garlic, and red chili. Combine with 5g sea salt and juice of half lime. Place in a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess achieved. Taste daily. Refrigerate when ready.

Prepare ginger-fennel oil: Finely chop remaining ginger peels and fennel fronds. Heat 50 ml vegetable oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add chopped ginger and fennel. Infuse gently for 15-20 minutes. Do not brown. Strain oil. Discard solids. Set oil aside.

Prepare vegetables: Peel and dice carrots, potatoes, and fennel bulb into 1 cm cubes. Blanch vegetables separately in boiling water until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Assemble soup: Heat strained broth. Add maple syrup and honey. Season with salt and pepper. Add blanched carrots, potatoes, and fennel to the warm broth. Simmer for 2 minutes to heat through.

Serve: Ladle hot broth and vegetables into individual bowls. Place a spoonful of fermented tomato relish in the center of each bowl. Drizzle with ginger-fennel oil. Garnish with a few fresh fennel fronds or finely chopped carrot greens if available.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Carrot & Ginger Beef Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of soup is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a natural off-white tone. The broth is a rich, clear amber-brown, revealing tender, irregularly cut 3-4 cm beef chunks, alongside roasted potato and carrot pieces with subtly caramelized edges. A few translucent, pale orange and yellow slices of fermented carrot and ginger are thoughtfully placed on the surface. A sprig of fresh green fennel fronds and a few delicate carrot greens are arranged simply, adding a vibrant contrast. The composition is clean and unfussy, highlighting the natural textures and earthy colors of the ingredients. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly placed to one side. Soft, diffused natural lighting illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows and emphasizing the wholesome, unadorned beauty of the soup. The background is minimalist, with a blurred hint of natural plant foliage or a simple white wall, ensuring the focus remains entirely on the dish.

ingredients.name: Beef stewing cuts (e.g., chuck, short rib)
Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (2 for fermenting, 2 for roasting, plus ends for stock)

instructions: Prepare beef stock: Place beef bones, carrot ends, tomato scraps, fennel trimmings, 2 garlic cloves, and 20g ginger in a large pot. Cover with 2 litres of water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 4-6 hours. Strain broth. Discard solids.

For fermented carrots and ginger: Thinly slice 2 carrots and 50g ginger. Pack tightly into a clean 500ml jar. Dissolve 10g sea salt in 500ml filtered water to make a 2% brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until pleasantly tart. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Cut beef into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Dice remaining 3 garlic cloves, 10g ginger, and chili. Dice fennel bulb. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pot. Sauté diced garlic, ginger, chili, and fennel bulb until softened, about 5 minutes.
Dice 3 tomatoes. Add diced tomatoes to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until softened. Deglaze with juice of 1/2 lemon.

Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in strained beef stock. Add maple syrup, honey, dried apricots, and dried plums. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender.

Meanwhile, cut potatoes and remaining 2 carrots into 2-3 cm chunks. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Remove apricots and plums from the soup. They will have imparted their flavor. Discard.
Add roasted potatoes and carrots to the soup. Stir in juice of 1/2 lime and remaining 1/2 lemon. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
To serve: Ladle soup into individual bowls. Top each serving with a few pieces of fermented carrot and ginger. Garnish with fresh fennel fronds and any reserved carrot greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl holds a generous portion of hearty soup. It features tender, braised beef in 2-3 cm cubes, with 2 cm chunks of diced carrots and potatoes. Thinly sliced, softened fennel pieces are visible throughout the rich, warm reddish-brown broth, which is slightly thickened. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A plain cloth napkin is casually placed beside it. Natural, soft lighting from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The background suggests a lived-in family kitchen, with subtle hints of everyday items. The presentation is homely and comforting.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 2-3 cm cubes. Peel and cut carrots and potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Deseed and finely chop chili. Trim and thinly slice fennel bulb.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add sliced fennel to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and chopped chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef stock and canned diced tomatoes. Scrape bottom of pot to loosen any browned bits.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add chopped carrots and potatoes. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is tender.
Stir in maple syrup, honey, lime juice, and lemon juice. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust chili to desired spice level.
Soup tastes even better the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Egg Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous individual portion of vibrant Chicken and Egg Fried Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned on a simple wooden table surface. The dish showcases fluffy, individual grains of golden-hued jasmine rice, subtly toasted from stir-frying. Interspersed throughout are tender, lightly browned cubes of chicken, delicate scrambled egg pieces, and small, bright orange diced carrots alongside translucent diced onions. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with golden rice, brown chicken, yellow egg, and orange carrots, all flecked with green from freshly sliced green onions as a garnish. The ingredients are evenly distributed, creating a balanced and appealing composition with moderate negative space around the edges of the plate. The rice is loose and free-flowing, not compacted. A pair of polished wooden chopsticks rests to the right of the plate, and a small, white ceramic rice bowl is placed slightly above, hinting at traditional East Asian dining. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is positioned to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures of the rice and vegetables, against a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of soy sauce or chili oil for individual seasoning.
Offer pickled daikon or cucumber as a refreshing counterpoint.
instructions: Prepare ingredients. Dice chicken, onion, and carrots. Mince garlic and grate ginger. Beat eggs.

Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add diced chicken. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add diced onions and carrots. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Push vegetables to one side of the wok. Pour beaten eggs into the empty space. Scramble eggs gently until just set. Break into small pieces.
Add cold cooked rice to the wok. Break up any clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes, tossing constantly, until rice is heated through and slightly toasted.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Pour soy sauce and sesame oil over the rice. Season with salt and white pepper.
Continue stir-frying for 2-3 minutes, ensuring all ingredients are well combined and heated through.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with sliced green onions.
notes: Using day-old, cold rice is crucial for achieving distinct, non-clumpy grains.
Adjust soy sauce to taste; some prefer more or less.
The chicken should be diced into uniform 1.5 cm cubes for even cooking and presentation.
Carrots should be diced finely (0.5 cm) so they cook quickly and blend well.
traditional_techniques: Stir-frying (wok hei concept for high heat cooking)

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Mozzarella Cannelloni
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Spinach and Mozzarella Cannelloni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table surface. Three to four cannelloni tubes, approximately 10-12 cm long, are arranged neatly side-by-side. The top layer of béchamel sauce and cheese is baked to a golden-brown, bubbly perfection, with hints of creamy white béchamel visible around the edges. Melted mozzarella forms a delicate crust, and vibrant green flecks of finely chopped spinach are visible from the ends of the tubes or where the sauce has settled. A few fresh, whole basil leaves are artfully placed on top, adding a pop of dark green color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space on the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. Beside the plate, a polished silver fork and knife rest on a folded white cotton napkin. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, warm bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer a small bowl of extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Accompany with a simple mixed green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until wilted, about 3-5 minutes.
Transfer wilted spinach to a colander. Press firmly to remove all excess water. Finely chop the spinach.
In a large bowl, combine chopped spinach, ricotta cheese, 200g shredded mozzarella, 25g grated Parmigiano Reggiano, a pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well to create the filling.
Prepare the béchamel sauce: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk, a little at a time, to prevent lumps. Continue whisking until the sauce thickens and is smooth.
Season béchamel with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Remove from heat.
Spread a thin layer of béchamel sauce on the bottom of a 20x30 cm (8x12 inch) baking dish.
Carefully fill each cannelloni tube with the spinach and cheese mixture. Use a piping bag or a small spoon.
Arrange filled cannelloni tubes in a single layer in the baking dish.
Pour remaining béchamel sauce evenly over the cannelloni, ensuring all tubes are covered.
Sprinkle remaining 50g shredded mozzarella and 25g grated Parmigiano Reggiano over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure spinach is very well-drained after wilting; excess water will make the filling soggy.
If cannelloni tubes are difficult to fill, a piping bag or a zip-top bag with a corner snipped off can make the process easier.

recipes.recipe_name: Conchiglioni Ripieni con Spinaci e Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Conchiglioni Ripieni con Spinaci e Mozzarella is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Three generously stuffed pasta shells, golden-baked with bubbling, melted mozzarella, are nestled within a rich, vibrant red marinara sauce. The pasta shells are large and plump, showcasing the creamy, light green spinach and white mozzarella filling peeking from their openings. The sauce is thick and clings well to the pasta. A few fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the top as a garnish. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space around the dish. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an inviting, authentic Italian bistro atmosphere. No overcrowding, the focus is entirely on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a large baking dish.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook conchiglioni shells according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until wilted, about 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Squeeze excess water from the cooked spinach. Chop finely.
In a large bowl, combine chopped spinach, ricotta cheese, diced mozzarella, Parmigiano Reggiano, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper. Mix well until thoroughly combined.
Spread 250 ml of marinara sauce evenly over the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Carefully stuff each cooked conchiglioni shell with the spinach and cheese mixture. Fill generously.
Arrange the stuffed shells in a single layer in the baking dish. They should fit snugly.
Pour the remaining marinara sauce over the stuffed shells. Ensure all shells are covered with sauce.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is melted and lightly golden. For a browner top, broil for the last 2-3 minutes.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure the spinach is thoroughly drained to prevent a watery filling.
Do not overcook the pasta before stuffing; it will continue to cook in the oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Ethiopian Spiced Beef & Potato Kutlet
recipes.visual_description: The Ethiopian Spiced Beef & Potato Kutlet starter is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set on a simple wooden table. Two golden-brown, irregularly oval kutlets, approximately 7cm long and 1.5cm thick, are centrally placed. The kutlets have a subtly crisp, pan-fried exterior, revealing the rich, spiced beef and soft potato within. Beside the kutlets, a small, vibrant mound of fresh, finely diced red onion and tomato salad offers a bright contrast in color and texture. A scattering of fresh, chopped green coriander leaves garnishes the dish, providing a fresh aroma and pop of color. A small, neatly folded piece of spongy, pale Injera bread rests beside the main elements, ready for scooping. The overall plating is clean, balanced, and approachable, with adequate negative space. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's warm tones and inviting textures. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, completing the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve communally on a large injera for a shared experience.
Eat with hands, tearing off pieces of injera to scoop the kutlets and salad.
Traditionally accompanied by a small side of Awaze (berbere paste) for extra spice.
instructions: Boil potato cubes in salted water until tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large pan, heat 15ml Niter Kibbeh over medium heat. Add half of the finely diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add minced beef to the pan. Break up beef with a spoon. Cook until browned and no pink remains, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in berbere spice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, cooked beef mixture, fresh breadcrumbs, and beaten egg. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix well until combined.
Divide mixture into 8 equal portions. Form each portion into a small, flat, oval-shaped kutlet (patty), about 1.5cm thick.

In a clean pan, heat remaining 15ml Niter Kibbeh over medium heat. Fry kutlets in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C for beef.
For the salad: In a small bowl, combine remaining finely diced red onion, finely diced tomato, and half of the chopped fresh coriander. Mix gently.
To serve: Place two kutlets on each plate. Spoon a small amount of the fresh onion-tomato salad beside the kutlets. Garnish with remaining fresh coriander. Serve with a small folded piece of injera.
traditional_techniques: Use of Niter Kibbeh (spiced clarified butter)
Layering of Berbere spice with aromatics

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Apple and Chickpea Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: The Spiced Apple and Chickpea Pilaf is presented in a pristine, shallow white porcelain bowl, forming a gently mounded, inviting portion. The dish showcases a harmonious blend of textures and colors: fluffy basmati rice and hearty wild rice grains are clearly visible, interspersed with tender, golden-brown diced apples and creamy, light-brown chickpeas. Finely chopped fresh green parsley is generously scattered over the top, providing a vibrant color contrast and herbaceous aroma. Toasted slivered almonds add a subtle crunch and nutty finish, glistening slightly. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the pilaf, inviting the viewer to focus on the dish's rich composition. A simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting enhance the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or a simple fresh herb salad with olives.
Accompany with warm flatbread.
instructions: Rinse wild rice blend and basmati rice separately under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well.
Dice yellow onion into small cubes. Mince garlic cloves.
Dice apples into 1.5 cm cubes, removing core.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed wild rice blend and basmati rice to the pot. Stir to coat grains with spices. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is nearly tender.
Stir in drained chickpeas and diced apples. Re-cover. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, until apples are tender-crisp and rice is fully cooked.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff pilaf gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and toasted slivered almonds before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork and Salmon Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Spicy Pork and Salmon Fritters are casually piled on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The fritters are round, about 5 cm in diameter, with a golden-brown, slightly crispy exterior from pan-frying. Their surfaces reveal flecks of red from diced tomato and vibrant green from finely chopped herbs within the mixture. Some fritters are slightly overlapping, creating a natural, unpretentious stack. A few fresh lemon wedges are placed alongside, ready to be squeezed. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showing subtle grain and natural imperfections. A simple, casually folded linen napkin in a neutral tone rests nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft lighting, typical of a cozy family kitchen, highlighting the natural textures and inviting appearance of the homemade snack. Portions are generous, suitable for sharing. No decorative elements, just the food and its simple accompaniments.
instructions: Dice salmon into small cubes.
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, diced salmon, diced onion, minced garlic, diced tomato, chili flakes, lemon zest, egg, and breadcrumbs.
Season with salt and pepper.
Mix well until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form mixture into 12 small, flat fritters, about 5 cm in diameter.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Fry fritters for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure pork reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove fritters from pan. Drain on paper towels.
Drizzle with fresh lemon juice before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Panang Hake Soup with Fermented Lemon
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Sustainable Panang Hake Soup is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with an organic, natural aesthetic. The bowl is a soft cream or beige tone, reflecting traditional pottery. The creamy, light orange-hued soup fills the bowl, showcasing its smooth texture. Generous, flaky chunks of poached hake are nestled in the soup, maintaining their natural form, not sliced. Vibrant green blanched tatsoi leaves are artfully arranged around the hake, providing a fresh color contrast. Two perfectly halved soft-boiled eggs, revealing their rich yellow yolks, are placed on the edge of the soup. A delicate sprinkle of pale yellow Fermented Lemon Rind Powder graces the surface of the soup and eggs, adding a subtle textural element. The setting features a light, natural wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually placed beside the bowl. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the dish to be the focal point, with soft, natural lighting enhancing the ingredients' pure beauty. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a comforting main dish.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Lemon Rind Powder: Thoroughly wash and dry 1 lemon. Remove zest in wide strips. Ferment zest in a small jar with a pinch of salt and enough water to cover for 3-5 days. Drain, pat dry, then dehydrate until brittle. Grind into a fine powder.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Add panang curry paste. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Add jasmine tea leaves directly to the simmering broth. Steep for 5 minutes. Strain out tea leaves.
Cut hake fillets into 4-5 cm chunks. Gently add hake chunks to the simmering soup. Poach for 5-7 minutes until cooked through and flaky. Do not overcook.
Blanch tatsoi: Briefly immerse tatsoi leaves in boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Gently squeeze out excess water.
Boil eggs: Cook eggs for 6-7 minutes for a soft-boiled yolk. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Peel carefully. Cut each egg in half lengthwise.
Stir in fresh lemon juice from half a lemon into the soup. Season with salt to taste.
Ladle soup into individual bowls. Arrange hake chunks and blanched tatsoi leaves artfully in each bowl.
Place two egg halves per bowl. Garnish each serving with a sprinkle of Fermented Lemon Rind Powder and a few fresh tatsoi leaves.
notes: The vegetable broth can be made using saved vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends) to minimize waste.
Adjust the amount of panang curry paste to your preferred spice level.
The Fermented Lemon Rind Powder can be prepared in advance and stored in an airtight container.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Parmesan Risotto with Poached Egg and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Parmesan risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is spread naturally on the plate, forming a shallow, fluid pool, exhibiting its rich, velvety texture and pale golden hue. A perfectly poached egg, with its glistening white and bright yellow yolk, rests gently in the center of the risotto. Around the base of the risotto, vibrant green asparagus spears are arranged neatly. A light sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh parsley adds subtle color and texture. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a clean white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, unobtrusive background that suggests a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Heat vegetable stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Melt 30 g butter with olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced shallot. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each ladle to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
The risotto should be creamy and al dente. Remove from heat.
Stir in remaining 30 g butter and 80 g grated Parmesan. Stir vigorously to create a creamy texture (mantecatura). Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a separate pot of salted water to a gentle simmer for the eggs.
Carefully crack each egg into a small bowl. Gently slide each egg into the simmering water. Poach for 3-4 minutes for a runny yolk.
Blanch asparagus spears in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain immediately and refresh in ice water to retain color and crispness. Drain well.
Divide risotto among four warm plates. Ensure the risotto spreads naturally, forming a fluid base.
Place one poached egg gently on top of each risotto portion.
Arrange blanched asparagus spears neatly beside the risotto.
Garnish with remaining grated Parmesan and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Gobi Aur Brussels Sprout Bhuna
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Roasted cauliflower florets and halved brussels sprouts, bearing slight caramelization and vibrant green-gold hues, are gently arranged in the center. They are coated in a rich, thick, deep reddish-brown bhuna masala, showcasing speckles of finely cooked onion and aromatic spices. The sauce clings to the vegetables, highlighting their distinct shapes and textures – tender-crisp florets and slightly charred sprout halves. A sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped coriander leaves provides a fresh counterpoint. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing the dish to be the focal point. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and a single individual portion. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its rich colors and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread, roti, or basmati rice.
Accompanied by a side of plain yogurt (dahi) or raita.
A wedge of fresh lime for squeezing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss cauliflower florets and halved brussels sprouts with 30 ml oil and a pinch of salt.
Spread vegetables on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Vegetables should be tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Heat remaining 30 ml oil in a large karahi or heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add sliced onion. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato puree. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oil separates from the mixture.
Add coriander powder, turmeric powder, and red chili powder. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly. Add a splash of water if mixture becomes too dry.
Add roasted cauliflower and brussels sprouts to the pan. Gently toss to coat with the masala.
Add 100-150 ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in garam masala and crushed kasuri methi. Cook for 1 minute.
Season with salt.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves.
notes: Adjust green chili and red chili powder to desired spice level.
Ensure vegetables are roasted to tender-crisp for best texture.
The bhuna process is key for deep flavor development.

recipes.recipe_name: Brussels Sprout and Bell Pepper Masala
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Brussels Sprout and Bell Pepper Masala is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, reddish-brown masala gravy, thick and fragrant, coats the tender Brussels sprouts, halved to expose their inner layers, and diced mixed bell peppers in shades of red, green, and yellow. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped coriander leaves garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The dish is mounded naturally, allowing for appropriate negative space on the plate. Beside the plate, a small white bowl of fluffy Basmati rice sits, accompanied by a piece of folded naan bread. The setting is a simple wooden table, illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a cotton napkin placed beside the plate.
instructions: Trim Brussels sprouts. Halve larger sprouts. Dice bell peppers into 1.5 cm pieces. Finely chop onions. Mince garlic and ginger to a paste. Dice tomatoes.
Heat oil or ghee in a large pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Let them crackle for 30 seconds.
Add chopped onions. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes and salt. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Brussels sprouts and diced bell peppers to the pan. Sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in water. Bring to a simmer. Cover the pan. Cook for 10-12 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in garam masala and kasoori methi. Cook for 2 minutes uncovered.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Tartaletas de Limón con Crujiente de Salmón Dulce
recipes.visual_description: Four individual golden-baked tartlets rest on a clean white porcelain plate, arranged with moderate negative space. Each tartlet features a vibrant, pale yellow lime curd filling. Above the curd, glossy white meringue peaks are delicately torched to a light golden-brown, creating a visually appealing contrast. Thin, translucent, and slightly reddish-orange candied salmon crisps are artfully placed upright into the meringue, acting as the primary visual focal point. The tartlet crusts are crisp and uniformly golden. A subtle scattering of fresh lime zest adds a touch of green. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with balanced colors and textures. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a traditional fork, illuminated by natural, even lighting from the side, creating a modern bistro ambiance with a hint of Mexican flair. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a dessert or with a small cup of café de olla.
Offer small shot glasses of Tequila or Mezcal as an after-dinner digestif.
instructions: Prepare the sweet pastry dough: Combine flour, cold butter, and a pinch of salt in a food processor. Pulse until crumbly. Add egg yolks and 50g granulated sugar. Pulse until dough forms. Wrap dough in plastic, chill 30 minutes.
Roll out dough to 3 mm thickness. Cut into 4 circles. Press into 10 cm tartlet molds. Prick bottoms with a fork. Chill 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line tart shells with parchment paper. Fill with baking beans. Blind bake 15 minutes. Remove beans and parchment. Bake 5-7 minutes more until golden. Cool shells completely.

Prepare the lime curd: Whisk lime juice, 100g granulated sugar, and whole eggs in a saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, whisking constantly, until thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in 25g cold unsalted butter and lime zest until smooth. Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve. Cover with plastic wrap touching surface. Chill until firm.

Prepare the sweet salmon crisp: Slice salmon fillet very thinly, 1 mm thick. Aim for 4-6 small pieces per tartlet. Bring 50g granulated sugar and 100 ml water to a simmer. Add a pinch of salt. Remove from heat. Dip salmon slices briefly in the warm simple syrup. Place salmon slices on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Preheat oven to 100°C. Bake salmon slices for 45-60 minutes, or until crisp and slightly translucent. Cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
Prepare the meringue: Whisk egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add caster sugar, one tablespoon at a time. Whisk until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Assemble the tartlets: Fill cooled tartlet shells with chilled lime curd. Pipe or spoon meringue over the curd, creating peaks.
Torch the meringue lightly with a kitchen torch until golden brown. Arrange 2-3 sweet salmon crisps artistically on top of each tartlet. Serve immediately.
notes: Using fresh lime juice and zest is crucial for authentic Mexican flavor.
The salmon crisp provides a unique textural and visual element; its sweetness should be subtle to complement the tartlet.
Ensure tartlet shells are fully cooled before filling to prevent the curd from melting.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chicken with Creamy Corn and Peas
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a modest, round, off-white ceramic plate. Surrounding the chicken is a rich, creamy pale yellow sauce, generously studded with vibrant green peas and bright yellow corn kernels. The sauce is fluid, naturally pooling around the chicken, with some overlapping onto its surface. The chicken exhibits a visible, crisp sear. The dish is presented on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. A simple, casually folded cream-colored cloth napkin is placed to the side, along with a standard fork and knife. The lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting a cozy family kitchen atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in home environment. The plate is adequately filled, showcasing a comforting, hearty portion without being overcrowded.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes
Serve with steamed rice
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring the sauce to a simmer, stirring, until it thickens.
Add frozen green peas and corn kernels to the sauce. Cook for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Return cooked chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over the chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Tomato Confit, Caramelized Onion Soubise, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly seared, golden-skinned chicken breast, presented whole and unsliced, rests elegantly atop a creamy, pale gold caramelized onion soubise, artfully spread with a soft, organic sweep across the pristine white bone china plate. Scattered around the chicken are vibrant, ruby-red confit cherry tomato halves, their slightly wrinkled skins contrasting with their plump interiors. A glossy, deep amber chicken jus forms a delicate pool at the base of the chicken, enhancing its rich color. The minimalist composition features ample negative space, highlighting the precise cooking and premium ingredients. A few delicate sprigs of bright green micro basil are precisely placed for a final touch of freshness and color. The setting is a luxurious, grey-veined marble surface with a pristine white linen napkin folded in a precise triangle, creating a sophisticated and refined culinary experience.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Jus: Reduce chicken stock in a saucepan over medium heat until it coats the back of a spoon. This takes about 20-30 minutes. Set aside.

Make Caramelized Onion Soubise: Slice yellow onions thinly. Melt 25g butter with 1 tbsp olive oil in a pot over low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very soft. Do not brown. Add 50ml water if drying out. Blend caramelized onions with shallot, remaining 25g butter, and heavy cream until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.

Prepare Tomato Confit: Preheat oven to 150°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish. Add 50ml olive oil, 2 sprigs thyme, 2 crushed garlic cloves, pinch of salt. Roast for 45-60 minutes until softened and slightly shriveled.

Cook Chicken Breast: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 1 tbsp butter to the pan. Baste chicken with pan juices and butter. Cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous dollop of warm caramelized onion soubise onto the center of each plate. Place one whole chicken breast on top of the soubise. Arrange several confit cherry tomato halves artfully around the chicken. Drizzle chicken jus around the plate. Garnish with micro basil or chervil, if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: The soubise can be made ahead and gently reheated.
Achieving a deeply caramelized onion soubise is key for flavor depth.
Resting the chicken is crucial for juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce, Parmesan Polenta, and Beef Medallions
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain dinner plate holds a harmoniously arranged single serving. Centered on the plate is a golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, its skin crispy and glistening. Beside it, a perfectly seared, small beef tenderloin medallion, showcasing a rich, dark crust. A creamy, pale-beige mushroom and thyme sauce is artfully spooned over a portion of the chicken, with some pooling elegantly around its base. Adjacent to the proteins, a soft, pale yellow mound of creamy Parmesan polenta provides a comforting anchor. Fresh green thyme sprigs are thoughtfully placed atop the chicken and sauce, adding a vibrant color contrast and aromatic touch. A few delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese are scattered over the polenta. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its textures and rich, natural colors without harsh shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: beef tenderloin, cut into 4 small medallions

instructions: Prepare Polenta: Bring 750ml water and a pinch of salt to a boil in a saucepan. Gradually whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, until thickened and creamy, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in 50g grated Parmesan and 20g butter. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Sear Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season skin generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear until deep golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F), about 10-15 minutes. Remove from oven. Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.

Cook Mushrooms & Sauce: While chicken cooks, add 15g butter to the same skillet (after removing chicken). Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced shallot and chopped thyme. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant. Deglaze pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Finish Sauce: Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by one-third. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Sear Beef Medallions: Heat 15ml olive oil in a separate small skillet over high heat. Season beef medallions with salt and pepper. Sear 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Rest 2 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous portion of Parmesan polenta onto each plate. Place a seared chicken breast beside the polenta. Arrange a beef medallion next to the chicken. Spoon creamy mushroom sauce generously over chicken and around the plate. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs and a few shavings of Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic Confit and Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of seared beef medallions with garlic confit is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick, oval-shaped beef medallions, showcasing a deep golden-brown crust and a pink medium-rare interior, are placed slightly overlapping. Beside them, two thin, golden-brown crostini slices are artfully arranged. Scattered around the beef are a few tender, whole garlic confit cloves, glistening with their infused oil. A subtle drizzle of dark balsamic glaze or a rich pan jus lightly streaks the plate. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley and a small sprig of fresh rosemary. The plate is centered on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a soft, unfocused background of a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Prepare garlic confit: Peel 20 garlic cloves. Place in a small saucepan. Cover with 250 ml olive oil. Simmer gently over low heat for 30-45 minutes until garlic is very tender and lightly golden. Do not brown. Remove from heat. Let cool in oil.

Prepare crostini: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette into thin, 1 cm thick rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet. Drizzle with a small amount of olive oil. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Prepare beef: Cut beef tenderloin into 8 thick medallions, approximately 50 g each. Pat dry with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper on all sides.

Sear beef: Heat 30 ml olive oil and 30 g butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves and rosemary and thyme sprigs to the pan. Once butter is foamy and fragrant, add beef medallions. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Rest beef: Transfer seared beef medallions to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.

Assemble: Arrange 2 seared beef medallions on each white porcelain starter plate. Place 2-3 crostini alongside. Spoon a few confit garlic cloves and a small drizzle of the confit oil over the beef. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Drizzle with balsamic glaze if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Heirloom Tomato Bruschetta
recipes.visual_description: Heirloom Tomato Bruschetta is artfully arranged on a rustic wooden serving board. Each toasted bread slice, golden brown and crisp, is topped with a vibrant mound of diced heirloom tomatoes, showcasing a spectrum of red, orange, and yellow hues. Finely minced garlic is visible, interspersed with bright green chiffonade basil. A light sheen of high-quality extra virgin olive oil coats the tomatoes, catching the light. A delicate drizzle of dark balsamic glaze provides a contrasting accent. The presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space on the board. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a relaxed bistro atmosphere. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the board. Multiple bruschetta pieces are displayed for sharing, inviting casual enjoyment.
instructions: Dice heirloom tomatoes into small cubes. Place in a medium bowl.
Mince two garlic cloves finely. Add to diced tomatoes.
Chiffonade fresh basil leaves. Add to tomato mixture.
Pour 45 ml of extra virgin olive oil over tomatoes. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Stir gently to combine.
Slice baguette or ciabatta into 1.5 cm thick pieces.
Heat a grill pan or oven to medium-high. Toast bread slices until golden brown and crisp on both sides.
Cut remaining garlic clove in half. Rub cut side of garlic over one side of each toasted bread slice.
Spoon generous amounts of tomato mixture onto each toasted bread slice.
Arrange bruschetta on a serving platter or wooden board.
Drizzle lightly with balsamic glaze and remaining 15 ml of extra virgin olive oil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Mole Verde de Pistacho y Azafrán
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo con Mole Verde de Pistacho y Azafrán is presented on a clean white ceramic plate. Two or three succulent, whole chicken thigh pieces, rich golden-brown from searing, are nestled together, generously coated with the vibrant, velvety green mole sauce. The mole, infused with saffron, has subtle golden undertones and a smooth, thick texture. Alongside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy, pale green cilantro-lime rice provides a fresh contrast. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh coriander sprigs and a sprinkle of toasted, roughly chopped pistachios, adding texture and a pop of color. The setting is a modern bistro table with a warm wooden surface, a crisp white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and a traditional Mexican glass for water in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, with moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the mole.
Accompany with a side of pickled red onions for acidity.
Offer fresh lime wedges for an optional citrus zest.
Pair with a refreshing agua fresca, such as horchata or jamaica.
instructions: Preheat oven grill to high. Arrange tomatillos, onion quarters, garlic cloves, and jalapeño peppers on a baking tray. Grill for 10-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred and softened. Peel garlic.

Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season chicken thighs with salt. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) later when simmering in sauce.

In a blender, combine roasted tomatillos, onion, peeled garlic, jalapeños, pistachios, fresh coriander, saffron, ground cumin, Mexican oregano, and 250 ml chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. Add more broth if needed to achieve a pourable consistency.

Pour the mole verde into the same pot used for chicken. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly to prevent sticking. Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-35 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender, reaching 75°C (167°F). Stir occasionally.

While mole simmers, prepare cilantro-lime rice. Rinse rice until water runs clear. In a saucepan, combine rice with 500 ml water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork. Stir in juice of half a lime and 20 g fresh chopped coriander.

Taste mole and adjust salt as needed. Serve chicken pieces generously coated in mole verde, alongside a portion of cilantro-lime rice. Garnish with fresh coriander sprigs and a few toasted pistachios.
traditional_techniques: Tatemar (roasting vegetables on a comal or grill for char and depth)
Mole preparation (complex sauce layering and blending)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente penne pasta forms the base, generously coated in a rich, creamy mushroom sauce. Pan-seared chicken breast, cut into thick, irregular chunks, is nestled atop the pasta, displaying a golden-brown crust. Vibrant roasted broccoli florets, slightly charred, are arranged alongside the pasta. The creamy sauce incorporates golden-brown sautéed mushrooms and deep amber caramelized onions. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley and grated Parmesan cheese garnishes the dish. It rests on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware beside it, under soft, natural lighting. The plating is clean, balanced, and inviting, showcasing fresh ingredients.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Slice onion thinly. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add sliced onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized.
While onions caramelize, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add penne pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet for 10-15 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Slice mushrooms. Add 15g butter to the pan with caramelized onions. Increase heat to medium. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and golden.
Add minced garlic to the pan with mushrooms and onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Stir for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock until smooth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and half of the grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooked chicken chunks and drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water.
Serve pasta immediately, topped with roasted broccoli florets, remaining grated Parmesan, and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl on a rustic wooden table. Orecchiette pasta shells are tossed with 3cm irregular chunks of seared Italian sausage and vibrant green broccoli rabe florets. Small wedges of red bell pepper and sliced cremini mushrooms provide color contrast. Julienned sun-dried tomatoes add flecks of deep crimson. The sauce is a light, translucent emulsion of olive oil and garlic, coating each ingredient with a gentle sheen. A dusting of coarse, golden-brown toasted breadcrumbs and fresh oregano leaves is concentrated in the center. The arrangement is natural and organic, showing balanced portions with visible negative space around the inner rim of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Primitivo or Negroamaro wine
Provide extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
instructions: Bring 4 liters of heavily salted water to a boil.
Blanch broccoli rabe for 2 minutes until bright green. Remove and shock in ice water. Drain and chop into 5cm pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a pan. Add breadcrumbs and half the oregano. Toast until golden and crisp. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat 20ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Break sausage into 3cm chunks and sear until browned.
Add mushrooms and bell peppers to the skillet. Sauté for 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and chili flakes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Boil orecchiette in the same water used for broccoli rabe until al dente.
Reserve 150ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.
Add pasta and broccoli rabe to the skillet. Pour in reserved pasta water and remaining olive oil.
Toss vigorously over high heat for 1 minute to emulsify the sauce.
Season with salt and remaining oregano.
Divide into four bowls and top with toasted breadcrumbs.
notes: Do not overcook the broccoli rabe during the blanching stage to maintain its snap
Use high-quality bronze-die pasta for better sauce adhesion

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Red Curry Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai Red Curry Chicken portion rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Succulent, browned chicken chunks are nestled among bright red bell pepper strips, translucent onion wedges, and halved cherry tomatoes. The rich, creamy red-orange curry sauce generously coats all ingredients, pooling slightly at the base. Fresh green Thai basil leaves are scattered over the top, providing a fragrant and colorful garnish. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a small white rice bowl filled with fluffy jasmine rice, a fork, and a spoon, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small dish of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies) on the side for added spice.
Traditionally eaten with a fork and spoon, using the fork to push food onto the spoon.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Add red curry paste. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Stir well to combine with the paste.
Add palm sugar and fish sauce. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add kaffir lime leaves, red bell pepper strips, and onion wedges. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes and Thai basil leaves. Cook for 1 minute until basil wilts.
Remove kaffir lime leaves before serving. Serve hot with jasmine rice.
notes: Adjust red curry paste quantity to desired spice level.
Palm sugar can be substituted with brown sugar if unavailable.
traditional_techniques: Stir-frying curry paste to release aromatics.
Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: spicy, sour, sweet, and salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Pork Goulash
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hungarian Pork Goulash is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl. Thick, succulent chunks of braised pork, rich with a reddish-brown hue, are nestled among tender, vibrant red and green bell pepper strips and softened diced onions. The dish is enveloped in a glossy, thick, deep reddish-brown paprika-infused sauce. A small, creamy dollop of bright white sour cream crowns the center, garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped vivid green parsley. The composition is naturally arranged, allowing the rich colors and textures of the stew to dominate. The bowl rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin placed beside it. Lighting is soft, even, and natural, highlighting the warmth and depth of the dish. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere. A small, separate serving of traditional Hungarian nokedli (dumplings) or crusty bread is subtly visible beside the main bowl, completing the authentic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with nokedli (Hungarian dumplings)
Serve with boiled potatoes
Serve with crusty bread
Garnish with a dollop of sour cream
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 4-5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, sweet paprika, smoked paprika, and crushed caraway seeds. Stir constantly for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn the paprika.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add bell pepper strips, crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, and beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Uncover the pot for the last 30 minutes of cooking. This allows the sauce to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Remove bay leaf before serving.
Serve hot, garnished with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean & Roasted Corn Salad with Seared Beef
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. A base of dark black beans is generously topped with golden roasted corn kernels, bright red bell pepper dice, and delicate green cilantro. Small, seared beef cubes are interspersed throughout, adding a rich, savory note. Creamy, light green avocado chunks provide a soft contrast. The dish is finished with crumbles of white asadero cheese, lightly scattered over the top. A zesty lime vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, binding them together. The components are artfully arranged to be distinct yet harmonious, with moderate negative space. The beef is cubed, not fanned.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a small bowl of fresh Pico de Gallo or Salsa Roja on the side.

ingredients.name: Black Beans
ingredients.quantity: 2 cans (400 g each), rinsed and drained

ingredients.name: Fresh Corn
ingredients.quantity: 2 ears, kernels removed (or 300 g frozen corn)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss corn kernels with 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes, or until lightly charred. Let cool.

Pat beef dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef for 2-3 minutes per side until cooked to desired doneness. Internal temperature should reach 63°C for medium-rare. Rest beef for 5 minutes. Cut into small cubes.
In a large bowl, combine roasted corn, rinsed black beans, diced red bell pepper, finely diced red onion, chopped cilantro, and diced avocado.
For the dressing, whisk together 35 ml olive oil, lime juice, ground cumin, and chili powder in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Fold in seared beef cubes. Crumble asadero cheese over the top. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, use fresh corn and roast it until slightly caramelized.
Asadero cheese can be substituted with Oaxaca cheese or a mild mozzarella.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Fish with Chili Chocolate-Pineapple Sauce
