Each piece features a thick, golden-brown toasted bread slice, cut into a rustic, irregular shape. Piled generously atop each toast is a substantial portion of the Anasazi bean and beer mixture. The bean mixture is a rich, deep reddish-brown, exhibiting a comforting, chunky yet creamy texture with visible whole beans. A vibrant green sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh cilantro or parsley rests on top of each canapé, offering a fresh color contrast. The entire platter is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in soft, natural, warm lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. A casually placed, simple cloth napkin is visible nearby. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a homely kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of your favorite mild or medium hot sauce on the side for an optional spicy kick.
instructions: Rinse dried Anasazi beans. Soak overnight in cold water. Drain and rinse again.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add soaked and drained beans, beer, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer, partially covered, for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beans are very tender.
Mash about two-thirds of the beans directly in the pot with a potato masher, leaving some whole for texture. The mixture should be thick.
Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Slice the bread into 1.5 cm thick rounds or diagonal pieces.
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet. Toast in the oven for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp.
Spoon a generous amount of the warm bean mixture onto each toasted bread piece.
Garnish each toast with freshly chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Anasazi beans hold their shape well and develop a creamy interior. If not available, pinto beans can be substituted.
The bean mixture can be made ahead and reheated gently before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Anasazi Beans, Seared Duck Breast, Smoked Paprika Jus
recipes.visual_description: A refined, minimalist presentation on a round, off-white designer plate with abundant negative space, set on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. A free-form, artfully mounded portion of creamy, beer-braised anasazi beans forms the base, positioned slightly off-center. The beans appear tender and glossy. Two thick, diagonally cut pieces of seared duck breast, with deeply caramelized, crisp skin and a perfect medium-rare blush, are placed deliberately atop the bean mound. A rich, glossy smoked paprika jus is elegantly spooned around the base, creating a reflective pool. The dish is garnished with a delicate scattering of golden, ultra-thin crispy shallots for textural contrast, and a few vibrant microgreens, strategically placed for a pop of fresh color and height. A perfectly folded white linen napkin and polished silver flatware rest beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows, against an ultra-minimalist, dark background to emphasize the culinary artistry.
instructions: Soak anasazi beans overnight. Drain thoroughly.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season duck with salt and pepper.
Heat a cold, oven-safe pan over medium heat. Place duck breasts skin-side down. Render fat for 8-10 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh side for 2 minutes. Transfer pan to oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 55°C. Remove duck. Rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes.
For the beans: In a separate pot, heat olive oil. Sauté half of the diced shallots and minced garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.

Add drained anasazi beans, 250ml beer, 250ml chicken stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until beans are tender. Add more stock or water if needed to keep beans submerged. Season with salt and pepper.

For the smoked paprika jus: Pour off rendered duck fat, reserving 15ml. Deglaze duck pan with remaining 250ml beer, scraping up fond. Reduce by half. Add remaining 250ml chicken stock, remaining shallots, and smoked paprika. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Return to pan. Whisk in cold butter until emulsified and glossy. Season to taste.
For crispy shallots: Thinly slice one shallot into rings. Fry in reserved duck fat or olive oil until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.

To plate: Spoon a generous portion of beer-braised anasazi beans onto each plate. Slice rested duck breasts into thick, diagonal pieces. Place duck artfully on top of the beans. Drizzle smoked paprika jus around the dish. Garnish with crispy shallots and microgreens.
notes: Ensure beans are fully tender but not mushy; cooking time may vary based on bean age.
Resting the duck breast is crucial for juiciness and even cooking.
Cook duck to an internal temperature of 55°C (medium-rare) for optimal texture, or 75°C for well-done.

recipes.recipe_name: Fig and Honey Entremet with Crispy Ham
recipes.visual_description: A single Fig and Honey Entremet sits precisely centered on an elegant, pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The entremet is a perfect cylinder, coated in a glossy, translucent neutral glaze that subtly reflects light. Its surface reveals the delicate, light honey-golden hue of the mousse beneath. Atop the entremet, a single, thinly sliced fresh fig petal is meticulously placed, showcasing its vibrant purple-red skin and pale flesh. Around the base of the entremet, a scattering of fine, golden-brown crispy cured ham crumble provides a textural contrast. A delicate, curled strip of candied orange peel adds a pop of vibrant color and aromatic accent. The plate itself is impeccably clean, with ample negative space emphasizing the dessert's architectural form and refined simplicity. The setting features a polished white marble surface, with dramatic, directional lighting creating soft shadows that enhance depth. A precisely folded white linen napkin rests beside the plate, completing the haute patisserie shop aesthetic.

ingredients.name: For the Brown Butter Sable Breton
For the Fig and Orange Compote

instructions: Prepare the Brown Butter Sable Breton: Brown butter in a saucepan over medium heat until fragrant and amber. Cool slightly. Cream browned butter with sugar. Beat in egg yolk. Sift flour, baking powder, and salt. Add to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Form dough into a disc. Chill 30 minutes. Roll dough 5mm thick. Cut out 4 circles (7cm diameter). Bake at 170°C for 12-15 minutes until golden. Cool on rack.

Prepare the Fig and Orange Compote: Combine diced figs, orange zest, orange juice, and honey in a saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes. Figs should be soft and liquid reduced. Cool completely.

Prepare the Honey Mousse: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. In a saucepan, combine honey and water. Heat until honey dissolves. Whisk egg yolks in a bowl. Slowly temper yolks into the warm honey mixture. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened (82°C). Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into warm custard until dissolved. Strain custard. Cool to room temperature. Whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold cream into cooled custard in two additions. Fill individual entremet molds (6cm diameter, 4cm high) halfway with mousse. Pipe a layer of fig compote into the center. Top with more mousse. Smooth tops. Freeze for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Prepare the Crispy Cured Ham: Preheat oven to 160°C. Lay ham slices on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 8-12 minutes until very crisp. Cool completely. Crumble into small pieces.

Prepare the Neutral Glaze: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water. In a saucepan, combine water, sugar, and glucose syrup. Heat to 103°C. Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into hot syrup until dissolved. Cool glaze to 30-35°C.

Assemble the Entremets: Unmold frozen entremets. Place on a wire rack over a tray. Pour cooled glaze evenly over each entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess glaze drip. Carefully transfer glazed entremets to serving plates.

Garnish: Arrange one thin slice of fresh fig on each entremet. Sprinkle crispy ham crumble precisely around the base or on top. Add a small strip of candied orange peel. Optionally, place a tiny piece of edible gold leaf for final elegance. Serve immediately or keep chilled until serving.
notes: Precision in measurements and temperatures is crucial for entremet success, especially for the mousse and glaze.
Ensure entremets are fully frozen before unmolding and glazing for clean results.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Pineapple-Chocolate Black Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: The stew is presented in a deep, matte white ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, dark mahogany color. Large, tender black beans are suspended in a thick, glossy sauce. Interspersed are vibrant, charred wedges of roasted red and yellow bell peppers, alongside glistening, caramelized chunks of fresh pineapple. A vibrant scattering of fresh, roughly chopped cilantro leaves provides a fresh green contrast. A bright lime wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. The textures are varied: creamy beans, yielding peppers, and juicy pineapple. The dish is placed on a light wooden table surface, beside a folded natural linen napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's deep hues and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping.
Offer a side of fluffy white rice.
A dollop of plant-based crema or avocado slices can complement the richness.

ingredients.name: Dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher), finely chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut bell peppers into large wedges. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
Cut pineapple into 2 cm chunks. Set aside.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, vegetable stock, and chipotle in adobo. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in the chopped dark chocolate until fully melted and incorporated.
Add cooked black beans and pineapple chunks to the pot. Stir well. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. The stew should thicken slightly.
Stir in the roasted bell pepper wedges. Cook for another 5 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: Use a high-quality dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher) for the best flavor balance; avoid overly sweet chocolate.
Adjust the amount of chipotle in adobo to control the spice level according to preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Gebratener Zander, Kartoffelpüree, Zwiebelconsommé
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated Zander fillet rests elegantly on a pristine white, shallow bone china plate. The fish, pan-seared to perfection, boasts a golden-crisp skin, contrasting with its moist, pearlescent white flesh. Beside it, a single, perfectly formed quenelle of glossy, ultra-smooth Kartoffelpüree gleams, its pristine white color providing a soft counterpoint. A small, clear pool of amber Zwiebelconsommé encircles the elements, its transparency allowing the plate's white space to dominate. A delicate scattering of vibrant green snipped chives adds a precise touch of color and freshness atop the fish and puree. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space highlighting the architectural precision of each component. The plate sits on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle shadows, emphasizing the dish's refined simplicity. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, and modern designer flatware complete the ultra-minimalist, high-end setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Pair with a dry German Riesling or a crisp Silvaner wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Place quartered yellow onions and shallots on a baking tray. Roast for 30-40 minutes until deeply caramelized.
Transfer roasted onions and shallots to a large pot. Add vegetable stock, white wine, bay leaf, black peppercorns, and thyme. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer gently for 1 hour.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Let broth cool to room temperature.
For clarification, whisk egg whites with ice cubes until frothy. Gently fold into the cooled broth.
Place pot over medium-low heat. Slowly bring to a simmer without stirring. As egg whites coagulate, they form a raft. Simmer for 20-30 minutes until raft is solid.
Carefully create a small hole in the raft. Ladle crystal-clear consommé through a muslin-lined sieve into a clean pot. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 2 cm pieces. Place in a pot of cold, salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot, empty pot over low heat for 1 minute to dry excess moisture.
Pass hot potatoes through a potato ricer or food mill directly into a clean saucepan.
Gradually whisk in cold butter cubes until fully incorporated and puree is smooth and glossy.
Gradually whisk in hot milk until desired creamy consistency. Season with fine sea salt and a pinch of nutmeg. Keep warm over a bain-marie or very low heat.
Pat Zander fillets very dry. Score the skin lightly in 2-3 places. Season skin side generously with sea salt and white pepper. Lightly season flesh side.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place Zander fillets skin-side down in hot oil. Press gently to ensure full skin contact. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy.
Add butter to the pan. Baste the flesh side of the fish with melted butter.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Finish cooking for 3-5 minutes, until fish is cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63°C.
Carefully remove Zander from pan. Let rest for 1 minute.
Warm four shallow, wide plates. Place a neat, small quenelle or dollop of Kartoffelpüree slightly off-center on each plate.
Carefully place one Zander fillet, skin-side up, next to the potato puree.
Pour a small amount of warm Zwiebelconsommé around the base of the Zander and potato.
Garnish with a small sprinkle of finely snipped chives over the fish and puree. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure potatoes are very dry before ricing for the smoothest puree.
The consommé can be prepared a day in advance and gently reheated.
Patting the fish skin very dry is crucial for achieving crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Dark Beer Stew with Pea Potato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A robust and inviting Beef and Dark Beer Stew is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Rich, dark brown chunks of tender beef are nestled among soft, stewed carrots, onions, and celery, all coated in a glossy, thick sauce. The stew is mounded slightly, showcasing its hearty texture. Adjacent to the stew, a vibrant green scoop of creamy pea and potato puree provides a striking color contrast. The puree is smooth and artfully placed. A small, separate white bowl holds fluffy, perfectly steamed white rice, complementing the main dish. A fresh sprig of thyme or flat-leaf parsley is placed delicately on the stew as a garnish. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface with a neutral-colored cotton napkin folded neatly beside it. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the deep colors and textures of the ingredients. Standard silver flatware is arranged beside the plate.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3-4 cm chunks. Pat dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until well-browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring to coat vegetables.
Gradually pour in dark beer, scraping the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef stock, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender.

While stew simmers, prepare potato and pea puree. Place chopped potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold water and add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until fork-tender. Drain well.
Add frozen green peas to the hot potatoes. Let stand for 2 minutes to thaw. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Cook rice according to package instructions. Typically, combine 240g rice with 480ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Once beef stew is tender, remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle hot beef stew onto plates. Serve with a generous scoop of pea and potato puree alongside. Serve steamed rice in a separate small bowl.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Haricots Verts Salad with Pickled Shallots and Whole Grain Mustard Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant green broccoli and haricots verts salad is meticulously arranged on a pristine white bone china plate, resting on a cool grey veined marble surface. Small, perfectly blanched broccoli florets and thin slices of tender broccoli stem are artfully intertwined with crisp, slender haricots verts. Delicate, translucent rings of pickled purple shallots are interspersed throughout, adding a subtle color contrast. A luxurious, creamy whole grain mustard vinaigrette is artfully drizzled across the vegetables, with some pooling elegantly at the base. The composition is organic and flowing, with abundant negative space highlighting each component's precise preparation and vibrant color. A whisper of finely chopped fresh dill is scattered as a precise garnish. The scene is bathed in dramatic, professional lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance texture and depth. A precisely folded white linen napkin and minimalist flatware complete the ultra-minimalist background, emphasizing the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a selection of freshly baked, crusty German breads, such as Roggenbrot (rye bread) or Vollkornbrot (whole grain bread).
Pair with a crisp, dry German Riesling or a light, refreshing pilsner.
instructions: Prepare pickled shallots: Thinly slice shallots into rings. In a small saucepan, combine 60 ml white wine vinegar, 15 g sugar, and 5 g fine sea salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot pickling liquid over shallots in a heatproof bowl. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare vegetables: Cut broccoli into small, bite-sized florets. Peel and thinly slice any tender broccoli stems. Trim ends of haricots verts. Prepare a large bowl of ice water.

Blanch vegetables: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add broccoli florets and stem slices. Cook for 2 minutes. Add haricots verts. Cook for another 1-2 minutes, until vegetables are vibrant green and crisp-tender. Immediately transfer blanched vegetables to the ice bath to stop cooking. Drain thoroughly and pat dry.

Make vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together whole grain mustard, Dijon mustard, and 30 ml white wine vinegar. Slowly drizzle in 100 ml extra virgin olive oil while continuously whisking until a smooth, emulsified vinaigrette forms. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.

Assemble salad: In a large bowl, gently combine the blanched broccoli, haricots verts, and drained pickled shallots. Drizzle with most of the vinaigrette and gently toss to coat. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Plate and serve: Arrange the salad artfully on individual serving plates, creating an organic, flowing composition. Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh dill. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure vegetables are blanched just until crisp-tender to maintain their vibrant color and slight bite, then immediately shocked in ice water to stop cooking.
Patting the vegetables thoroughly dry after shocking is crucial for the vinaigrette to adhere properly and prevent dilution.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Chili-Mustard Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned pan-seared chicken thigh, its exterior a rich golden-brown, sits centrally on a round, cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate. The chicken is presented whole, a natural and robust form, not sliced. Alongside, vibrant green broccolini florets and stalks are artfully arranged, showcasing their natural shape and tender-crisp texture. A glossy, deep orange-red fermented chili-mustard glaze is artfully drizzled over the chicken and pools subtly around its base, adding a pop of color and liquid texture. Coarse, golden-brown sourdough crumbs are scattered thoughtfully over the chicken and plate, providing a rustic, crunchy counterpoint. A delicate, golden-brown cheddar crisp rests near the chicken, its irregular edges suggesting handmade artistry. The plate is positioned on a light, reclaimed wood table surface, revealing its natural grain. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually folded to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the left, highlighting textures and colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of natural elements like a leafy green plant, creating an eco-conscious, uncluttered aesthetic. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the components.
instructions: Prepare fermented chili base. Slice chilies. Mince garlic and ginger. Combine sliced chilies, minced garlic, grated ginger, 2g salt, 2g sugar, 60ml apple cider vinegar, and 60ml water in a clean jar. Seal loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 24 hours.
Make sourdough crumbs. Tear sourdough bread into small pieces. Toast in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and crisp. Crush or pulse into coarse crumbs. Set aside.

Prepare cheddar crisps. Preheat oven to 180°C. Grate cheddar cheese. Arrange small, thin piles of grated cheese on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until melted, bubbly, and golden brown. Cool completely on the baking sheet until crisp. Carefully remove. Set aside.

Cook broccolini. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Trim the tough ends from the broccolini. Blanch broccolini in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, until tender-crisp and vibrant green. Drain immediately. Set aside.

Cook chicken. Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken with remaining 3g salt and black pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs presentation side down for 6-8 minutes, until deeply golden brown and crisp. Flip chicken. Continue cooking for another 8-10 minutes, or until an internal temperature of 75°C is reached. Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Make glaze. Pour the fermented chili base (chilies, garlic, ginger, and liquid) into a blender. Blend until smooth. Stir in the Dijon mustard until fully combined.

Plate the dish. Place one rested chicken thigh on each handcrafted ceramic plate. Arrange a portion of blanched broccolini alongside the chicken. Drizzle generously with the fermented chili-mustard glaze over the chicken and around the plate. Sprinkle the sourdough crumbs over the chicken and broccolini. Place one crisp cheddar disc beside the chicken. Garnish minimally with fresh parsley or cilantro leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic beef and potato stew is presented in a deep, earthenware bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features generous chunks of tender, dark brown beef, nestled among soft, golden-yellow potato cubes, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and earthy brown quartered mushrooms. A rich, thick reddish-brown gravy coats all ingredients, with visible flecks of dried herbs. A light scattering of fresh green chopped parsley brightens the top. The stew has a comforting, slightly irregular texture, reflecting home cooking. The bowl sits on a simple ceramic plate. A linen napkin and a sturdy spoon are casually placed beside it. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onion and carrots to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually stir in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add potato cubes and quartered mushrooms. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30-40 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Buckwheat
recipes.special_requests: 130-150 grams of chicken,  50 grams of buckwheat groat - weight for dry, not cooked. Cook, stew, bake, fry without or on a drop of oil. We cook only chicken and buckwheat, proper nutrition for weight loss.
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of hearty chicken and buckwheat is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features tender, 2 cm cubed chicken pieces, lightly seared to a golden-brown, nestled amongst fluffy, cooked buckwheat groats. Diced orange carrots and softened white onion pieces are visibly mixed throughout, adding natural color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a vibrant contrast on top. The chicken is presented as whole chunks. The components are naturally intertwined, creating a comforting and wholesome appearance. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A basic, silver fork rests beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 2-3 minutes until lightly browned. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion and carrot to the same skillet. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add buckwheat groats, chicken broth, and dried thyme. Stir to combine.
Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until buckwheat is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Buckwheat Kasha
recipes.special_requests: 30-150 grams of chicken,  50 grams of buckwheat groat
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Chicken and Buckwheat Kasha is presented on a simple, round, rustic white ceramic plate. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, cooked to perfection, is placed centrally. The chicken piece is whole, showcasing its caramelized exterior. Beside it, a generous mound of fluffy buckwheat kasha, cooked to separate, tender groats, forms the base. Interspersed within the kasha are soft, translucent diced onions and tender diced carrots, adding natural sweetness and color. A sparse garnish of fresh chopped dill is sprinkled over the kasha, providing a vibrant green contrast. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Soft, inviting kitchen light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting textures and natural, earthy colors of the dish. A plain, silver fork lies casually beside the plate, completing the homely, unpretentious setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled vegetables, such as dill pickles or sauerkraut.
Often accompanied by a simple fresh cucumber and tomato salad.
instructions: Pat chicken thigh dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a medium pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thigh 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Dice onion and carrot into small cubes.
Add diced onion and carrot to the same pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add buckwheat groats to the pot. Toast 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and buckwheat is tender.
Remove pot from heat. Let kasha rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh dill.
Serve chicken thigh whole or cut into thick chunks over the buckwheat kasha. Garnish with chopped dill.
notes: For fluffier kasha, do not stir extensively during simmering.
Adjust liquid amount slightly if buckwheat is not fully tender after simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Shrimp Pasta with Peppers and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous home-style portion of Creamy Garlic Shrimp Pasta is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pasta is loosely twirled, forming a natural base. Cooked pinkish-orange shrimp are nestled on top and around the pasta. Tender, earthy brown sliced mushrooms and vibrant red diced bell pepper pieces are mixed throughout the creamy, light beige sauce that coats all components. Visible flecks of black pepper and bright green chopped parsley are scattered over the dish. The plate is adequately filled but not overflowing, allowing for some negative space around the edges. The dish rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, casually placed linen napkin and a fork are beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere in the slightly blurred kitchen background.
instructions: Cook pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 60 ml of pasta water.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and diced bell pepper. Cook 5-7 minutes until tender.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the pan. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from pan.
Pour chicken broth into the pan. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer 2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Return shrimp to the pan. Add cooked pasta. Toss to coat all ingredients with sauce. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
